title.zh: 卷四十二 蜀書十二 杜周杜許孟來尹李譙郤傳
title.en: Volume 42: Book of Shu 12 - Biographies of Du, Zhou, Du, Xu, Meng, Lai, Yin, Li, Qiao, and Xi
title.raw: 卷四十二 蜀書十二 杜周杜許孟來尹李譙郤傳 Volume 42: Book of Shu 12 - Biographies of Du, Zhou, Du, Xu, Meng, Lai, Yin, Li, Qiao, and Xi

sentences.zh: 杜微字國輔，梓潼涪人也。

translations.literal: Du Wei, courtesy name Guofu, was a man of Fu in Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: Du Wei, courtesy name Guofu, came from Fu in Zitong commandery.

sentences.zh: 少受學於廣漢任安。

translations.literal: In youth he received learning from Ren An of Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he studied under Ren An of Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 劉障辟為從事，以疾去官。

translations.literal: Liu Zhang summoned him as adjutant; because of illness he left office.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang appointed him adjutant, but illness forced him to resign.

sentences.zh: 及先主定蜀，微常稱聾，閉門不出。

translations.literal: When the First Lord pacified Shu, Wei constantly claimed deafness and closed his gate, not going out.
translations.idiomatic: After the First Lord conquered Shu, Wei feigned deafness and shut himself away.

sentences.zh: 建興二年，丞相亮領益州牧。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianxing, Chancellor Liang took concurrent post as shepherd of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianxing, Chancellor Zhuge Liang added the title of shepherd of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 選迎皆妙簡舊德，以秦宓為別駕，五梁為功曹，微為主簿。

translations.literal: In selection and welcome all were subtly chosen from old virtue, taking Qin Mi as chief clerk on tour, Wu Liang as merit assessor, and Wei as chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: His appointments favored established worthies: Qin Mi became chief clerk on tour, Wu Liang merit assessor, and Du Wei chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 微固辭，舉而致之。

translations.literal: Wei firmly declined; they raised him and brought him in.
translations.idiomatic: Wei refused repeatedly until they virtually escorted him to office.

sentences.zh: 既致，亮引見微，微自陳謝。

translations.literal: After he arrived, Liang led him in to an audience; Wei himself stated thanks and declined.
translations.idiomatic: Once there, Liang received him in audience; Wei apologized and begged off.

sentences.zh: 亮以微不聞人語，於坐上與書曰：

translations.literal: Because Wei did not hear human speech, Liang on the seat with him wrote saying,
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Wei could not hear conversation, Liang wrote him a note at the table:

sentences.zh: 服聞德行，飢渴歷時，清濁異流，無緣諮覯。

translations.literal: I have heard of your conduct and virtue, hungered and thirsted through the seasons; clear and turbid flow in different streams— without fate to consult and meet.
translations.idiomatic: I have long admired your character, yet our paths never crossed— like clear and muddy waters that never mingle.

sentences.zh: 王元泰、李伯仁、王文儀、楊季休、丁君乾、李永南兄弟、文仲寶等，每歎高志，未見如舊。

translations.literal: Wang Yuantai, Li Borun, Wang Wenyi, Yang Jixiu, Ding Junqian, Li Yongnan and his brothers, Wen Zhongbao, and others, each sighed at your lofty purpose, not having seen you as of old.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuantai, Li Borun, Wang Wenyi, Yang Jixiu, Ding Junqian, the Li Yongnan brothers, Wen Zhongbao, and the rest often spoke of your high aims and regretted losing touch.

sentences.zh: 猥以空虛，統領貴州，德薄任重，慘慘憂慮、朝廷主公今年始十八，天姿仁敏，愛德下士。

translations.literal: Meanly with empty vacuity I lead and govern your noble province; virtue is thin while the burden is heavy— I am miserable in worry and fear. The court's lord and master this year has only just reached eighteen; Heaven's endowment is humane and keen, loving virtue and lowering himself to knights.
translations.idiomatic: I govern this land with scant virtue and a crushing burden, anxious day and night. Our sovereign has only just turned eighteen— gifted, humane, and eager to honor men of talent.

sentences.zh: 天下之人思慕漢室，欲與君因天順民，輔此明主，以隆季興之功，著勳於竹帛也。

translations.literal: The people of the realm long for the house of Han; I wish with you, by Heaven and following the people, to aid this enlightened lord, thereby to enlarge the merit of restoring the late line and to inscribe deeds on bamboo and silk.
translations.idiomatic: All under Heaven yearn for Han. I hope you will join me in aiding this enlightened ruler, Heaven and the people willing, to rebuild the dynasty's fortunes and win a place in history.

sentences.zh: 以謂賢愚下相為謀，故自割絕，守勞而已，不圖自屈也。

translations.literal: I supposed worthy and foolish would not counsel each other below; therefore I myself cut off and broke ties, guarding my toil only, not planning to humble myself.
translations.idiomatic: I thought men of different gifts seldom counsel one another, so I kept my distance and minded my own office— I never meant to impose on you.

sentences.zh: 微自乞老病求歸，亮又與書答曰：

translations.literal: Wei himself begged old age and illness seeking return; Liang again with a letter answered saying,
translations.idiomatic: Du Wei pleaded age and infirmity and asked to retire. Liang wrote again:

sentences.zh: 曹丕篡弒，自立為帝，是猶土龍芻狗之有名也。

translations.literal: Cao Pi usurped and murdered, establishing himself as emperor— this is still a clay dragon or straw dog having a name.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi murdered his sovereign and stole the throne— a puppet emperor, as hollow as a clay dragon or a paper dog.

sentences.zh: 欲與羣賢因其邪偽，以正道滅之。

translations.literal: I wish with the assembled worthies, by means of his perverse falseness, with correct way to destroy him.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to join every able man in using his own treason to crush him with the righteous cause.

sentences.zh: 怪君未有相誨，便欲求還於山野。

translations.literal: I marvel that you, sir, have not yet given mutual instruction, then wish to seek return to mountain and wild.
translations.idiomatic: I am surprised you offer no counsel yet already seek the hills and forests.

sentences.zh: 丕又大興勞役，以向吳、楚。

translations.literal: Pi again greatly raised corvee labor, to march against Wu and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi has again launched vast levies against the southeast.

sentences.zh: 今因丕多務，且以閉境勤農，育養民物，並治甲兵，以待其挫，然後伐之，可使兵不戰民不勞而天下定也。

translations.literal: Now because Pi has many tasks, for the moment we close the borders, diligently farm, nurture and rear the people and things, and together repair armor and weapons, to await his setback, afterward to attack him— can cause the army not to fight, the people not to labor, and the realm to be settled.
translations.idiomatic: While he is overstretched, we should seal the passes, encourage farming, rest the people, and forge arms until his strength flags— then strike so that armies need not clash and the realm may be pacified without exhausting the common folk.

sentences.zh: 君但當以德輔時耳，不責君軍事，何為汲汲欲求去乎！

translations.literal: You, sir, only ought to aid the times with virtue; I do not demand military affairs of you— why urgently urgently wish to leave!
translations.idiomatic: I ask only that you lend the age your moral weight, not that you bear arms— why this desperate hurry to withdraw?

sentences.zh: 其敬微如此，拜為諫議大夫，以從其志。

translations.literal: His reverence for Wei was thus; he appointed him remonstrance counsellor, to follow his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Such was Liang's deference: he named Wei remonstrance counsellor and let him live as he wished.

sentences.zh: 五梁者，字德山，犍為南安人也，以儒學節操稱。

translations.literal: As for Wu Liang, courtesy name Deshan, a man of Nanan in Qianwei, he was famed for Confucian learning and integrity of conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Liang of Nanan in Qianwei, courtesy name Deshan, was known for scholarship and moral fiber.

sentences.zh: 從議郎遷諫義大夫、五官中朗將。

translations.literal: From master of discussion he was transferred to remonstrance grandee and general of the household in the five offices.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from master of discussion to remonstrance grandee and general of the household for the five offices.

sentences.zh: 周羣字仲直，巴西閬中人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Qun, courtesy name Zhongzhi, was a man of Langzhong in Ba commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Qun, courtesy name Zhongzhi, came from Langzhong in Ba commandery.

sentences.zh: 父舒，字叔布，少學術於廣漢楊厚，名亞董扶、任安。

translations.literal: His father Shu, courtesy name Shubu, in youth studied arts from Yang Hou of Guanghan; his name ranked below Dong Fu and Ren An.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhou Shu, courtesy name Shubu, studied under Yang Hou of Guanghan in youth and stood just below Dong Fu and Ren An in reputation.

sentences.zh: 數被徵，終不詣。

translations.literal: Several times he was summoned to office; in the end he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Court summoned him repeatedly; he never answered.

sentences.zh: 時人有問：「《春秋讖》曰『代漢者當塗高』，此何謂也？

translations.literal: Someone of the time asked: "The Spring and Autumn prophecy says, He who replaces Han will be dangtu gao— what does this mean?"
translations.idiomatic: A contemporary once asked how to read the prophecy, "He who replaces Han shall be High on the Road."

sentences.zh: 」舒曰：「當塗高者，魏也。

translations.literal: Shu said, "Dangtu gao is Wei."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shu answered, "High on the Road points to Wei."

sentences.zh: 」鄉黨學者私傳其語，羣少受學於舒，專心候業。

translations.literal: Village and district scholars privately transmitted his words; Qun in youth received learning from Shu, concentrating mind on prognostic arts.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars repeated his gloss in private. Zhou Qun studied under his father and devoted himself to celestial divination.

sentences.zh: 於庭中做小樓，家富多奴，常令奴更直於樓上視天災，才見一氣，即白羣，羣自上樓觀之，不避晨夜，故凡有氣候，無不見之者，是以所言多中。

translations.literal: In the courtyard he built a small tower; the household was rich with many slaves; he constantly ordered slaves in rotation on the tower to watch heavenly calamities; as soon as they saw one qi, they reported to Qun; Qun himself ascended the tower to observe it, not avoiding dawn or night; therefore whenever there was weather qi, there was none he did not see— for this reason what he spoke mostly hit.
translations.idiomatic: He put up a small tower in the courtyard and set slaves to watch the sky in shifts day and night. The moment a portent appeared they roused Qun, who climbed to study it himself. Because he missed nothing, his forecasts usually came true.

sentences.zh: 州牧劉璋辟以為師友從事。

translations.literal: The shepherd Liu Zhang summoned him as adjutant for teachers and friends.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang, as shepherd, named him adjutant for teachers and friends.

sentences.zh: 〈《續漢書》曰：建安七年，越巂有男子化為女人，時羣言哀帝時亦有此，將易代之祥也。

translations.literal: The Continued Book of Han states: In the seventh year of Jianan, in Yuexi a man transformed into a woman; at the time Qun said that in Emperor Ai's time there was also this— it will be an omen of changing the age.
translations.idiomatic: The Continued Han History records that in the seventh year of Jianan a man in Yuexi turned into a woman. Qun likened it to an omen from Emperor Ai's reign and called it a sign of dynastic change.

sentences.zh: 至二十五年，獻帝果封於山陽。

translations.literal: By the twenty-fifth year, the abdicated emperor was indeed enfeoffed at Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: By the twenty-fifth year of Jianan the abdicated emperor had indeed been enfeoffed at Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 十二年十月，有星孛於鶉尾，荊州分野，羣以為荊州牧將死而失土。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the twelfth year, a comet broomed the Quail's Tail, the field division of Jing Province; Qun thought the shepherd of Jing Province would die and lose his land.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the twelfth year of Jianan a comet swept the Quail's Tail asterism, Jing Province's celestial field. Qun predicted the death of Jing's shepherd and the loss of his territory.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，劉表卒，曹公平荊州。

translations.literal: The next autumn Liu Biao died; Lord Cao pacified Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn Liu Biao died and Cao Cao took Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 十七年十二月，星孛於五諸侯，羣以為西方專據土地者皆將失土。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the seventeenth year, a comet broomed the Five Feudatories; Qun thought all who monopolized land in the west would lose their soil.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the seventeenth year a comet crossed the Five Feudatories. Qun read it as doom for every western warlord who clung to territory.

sentences.zh: 是時，劉璋據益州，張魯據漢中，韓遂據涼州，宋建據枹罕。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Zhang held Yi Province, Zhang Lu held Hanzhong, Han Sui held Liang Province, Song Jian held Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang still held Yi, Zhang Lu Hanzhong, Han Sui Liangzhou, and Song Jian the Fuhan salient.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，曹公遣偏將擊涼州。

translations.literal: The next winter Lord Cao sent a detached general to strike Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: The next winter Cao Cao sent a column against Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 十九年，獲宋建，韓遂逃於羌中，被殺。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year they captured Song Jian; Han Sui fled among the Qiang and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year Song Jian was taken; Han Sui fled to the Qiang and died there.

sentences.zh: 其年秋，璋失益州。

translations.literal: That autumn Liu Zhang lost Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: That same autumn Liu Zhang lost Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 二十年秋，曹公攻漢中，張魯降。〉

translations.literal: In the twentieth autumn, Lord Cao attacked Hanzhong; Zhang Lu surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the twentieth year Cao Cao invaded Hanzhong and Zhang Lu yielded.

sentences.zh: 先主定蜀，署儒林校尉。

translations.literal: The First Lord pacified Shu and appointed him colonel of the forest of scholars.
translations.idiomatic: After the First Lord settled Shu he named Qun colonel of the forest of scholars.

sentences.zh: 先主欲曹公爭漢中，問羣，羣對曰：「當得其地，不得其民也，若出偏軍，必不利，當戒慎之！

translations.literal: When the First Lord wished to contend with Lord Cao for Hanzhong, he asked Qun; Qun replied saying, "You will obtain its land, you will not obtain its people; if you send a detached army, it will certainly be unfavorable— you must guard and be cautious!"
translations.idiomatic: Planning to wrest Hanzhong from Cao Cao, the First Lord asked Qun's opinion. Qun said, "You will take the ground but not the population. A detached column will fare badly— proceed with utmost care."

sentences.zh: 」時州後部司馬蜀郡張裕亦曉佔候，而天才過羣，

translations.literal: At that time the rear army marshal of the province, Zhang Yu of Shu commandery, also understood divination, while natural genius surpassed Qun,
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yu of Shu, the province's rear army marshal, was an even keener astrologer than Qun,

sentences.zh: 〈裕字南和。〉

translations.literal: Yu's courtesy name was Nanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yu's courtesy name was Nanhe.

sentences.zh: 諫先主曰：「不可爭漢中，軍必不利。

translations.literal: He remonstrated the First Lord saying, "You cannot contest Hanzhong; the army will certainly be unfavorable."
translations.idiomatic: He warned the First Lord, "Do not contest Hanzhong— the expedition will end badly."

sentences.zh: 」先主竟不用裕言，果得地而不得民也。

translations.literal: The First Lord in the end did not use Yu's words; indeed he obtained the land but did not obtain the people.
translations.idiomatic: The First Lord ignored Zhang Yu and, as predicted, won the terrain but not the people.

sentences.zh: 遣將軍吳蘭、雷銅等入成都，皆沒不還，悉如羣言。

translations.literal: He dispatched Generals Wu Lan, Lei Tong, and others on detached operations; all sank and did not return— entirely as Qun had said.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wu Lan, Lei Tong, and others on the detached columns; they were swallowed up without return— exactly as Zhou Qun had foretold.

sentences.zh: 於是舉羣茂才。

translations.literal: Thereupon they raised Qun as flourishing talent.
translations.idiomatic: Qun was then recommended as flourishing talent.

sentences.zh: 裕又私語人曰：「歲在庚子，天下當易代，劉氏祚盡矣。

translations.literal: Yu again privately told people saying, "In the year gengzi the realm ought to change its age; the Liu house's allotted span is exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yu also whispered that in the gengzi year the mandate would turn and the house of Liu would be finished.

sentences.zh: 主公得益州，九年之後，寅卯之間當失之。

translations.literal: The lord obtained Yi Province; after nine years, between yin and mao he ought to lose it."
translations.idiomatic: Our lord had taken Yi Province; within nine years, between the yin and mao branches, he would lose it."

sentences.zh: 」入密白其言。

translations.literal: Someone entered and secretly reported his words.
translations.idiomatic: An informer carried his words to the throne.

sentences.zh: 初，先主與劉璋會涪，時裕為璋從事，侍坐，其人饒須，先主嘲之曰：「昔吾居涿縣，特多毛姓，東西南北皆諸毛也，涿令稱曰『諸毛繞涿居乎』！

translations.literal: In the beginning, when the First Lord met Liu Zhang at Fu, at that time Yu was Zhang's adjutant, attending the seat; the man had abundant whiskers; the First Lord mocked him saying, "In old days I dwelt in Zhuo county— especially many with the surname Mao; east, west, south, and north were all various Mao; the magistrate of Zhuo said, Do the many Mao surround Zhuo dwelling!"
translations.idiomatic: Long ago, when the First Lord met Liu Zhang at Fu, Zhang Yu sat with Zhang's staff, heavily bearded. The First Lord teased him: "When I lived in Zhuo, every lane seemed full of Maos; the magistrate joked, The Maos wrap Zhuo on every side!"

sentences.zh: 」裕即答曰：「昔有作上黨潞長，遷為涿令者，去官還家，時人與書，欲署潞則失涿，欲署涿則失潞，乃署曰：『潞涿君』。

translations.literal: Yu immediately answered saying, "In old days there was one who was chief of Lu in Shangdang, transferred to be magistrate of Zhuo; leaving office and returning home, when people wrote to him, wishing to write Lu then lost Zhuo, wishing to write Zhuo then lost Lu— therefore he signed Lu-Zhuo lord."
translations.idiomatic: Yu shot back: "Once a man was magistrate of Lu in Shangdang and moved to Zhuo. Letters addressed to either place dropped the other title, so folk simply called him Lord Lu-Zhuo."

sentences.zh: 先主無須，故裕以此及之。

translations.literal: The First Lord lacked whiskers; therefore Yu by this reached him.
translations.idiomatic: The First Lord was beardless— Yu's barb hit its mark.

sentences.zh: 先主常銜莫不遜，加忿其漏言，乃顯裕諫爭漢中不驗，下獄，將誅之。

translations.literal: The First Lord constantly harbored resentment that he was not deferential, adding anger that he leaked words; therefore he displayed Yu's remonstrance contesting Hanzhong as unverified, cast him in prison, and would execute him.
translations.idiomatic: The First Lord never forgave the slight, and Yu's loose talk sealed his fate: his failed warning about Hanzhong was trumped up as false prophecy and he was jailed for execution.

sentences.zh: 諸葛亮表請其罪，先主答曰：「勞蘭生門，不得不鋤。

translations.literal: Zhuge Liang memorialized requesting his crime; the First Lord answered saying, "Weeds grow at the orchid's gate— they must be hoed."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang pleaded for him, but the First Lord answered, "When weeds spring beside the orchid, you have to cut them down."

sentences.zh: 」裕遂棄市。

translations.literal: Yu thereupon was cast away in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yu was executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 後魏氏之立，先主之薨，皆如裕所刻。

translations.literal: Later the Wei house's establishment and the First Lord's death were all as Yu had carved.
translations.idiomatic: Later events— Wei's rise and the First Lord's death— unfolded on the schedule Zhang Yu had scratched out.

sentences.zh: 又曉相術，每舉鏡視面，自知刑死，未常不撲之於地也。

translations.literal: He also understood physiognomy; each time he raised a mirror to view his face, he knew execution death— never did he fail to dash it to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: He also read faces: every time he lifted a mirror he saw his own doom and always hurled it down.

sentences.zh: 羣卒，子臣頗傳其術。

translations.literal: When Qun died, the son Chen somewhat transmitted his arts.
translations.idiomatic: After Qun died his son Zhou Chen inherited part of his craft.

sentences.zh: 杜瓊字伯瑜，蜀郡成都人也。

translations.literal: Du Qiong, courtesy name Boyu, was a man of Chengdu in Shu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Du Qiong, courtesy name Boyu, was a native of Chengdu in Shu commandery.

sentences.zh: 少受學於任安，精究安術。

translations.literal: In youth he received learning from Ren An and exhaustively investigated An's arts.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Ren An in youth and mastered Ren's methods.

sentences.zh: 劉璋時辟為從事，先主定益州，領牧，以瓊為議曹從事。

translations.literal: In Liu Zhang's time he was summoned as adjutant; when the First Lord pacified Yi Province and took the shepherd title, he made Qiong adjutant for the council chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang had appointed him adjutant; after the First Lord took Yi Province and the shepherd's seal, he made Qiong adjutant of the deliberation bureau.

sentences.zh: 後主踐阼，拜諫議大夫，遷左中郎將、大鴻臚、太常。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord ascended the throne, he was appointed remonstrance grandee, transferred to general of the left in the palace, grand herald, and grand master of ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Later Lord he rose from remonstrance grandee to general of the left in the palace, grand herald, and grand master of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 為人靜默少言，闔門自守，不與世事。

translations.literal: As a person he was quiet and silent, few in speech, closing his gate and guarding himself, not joining worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was a man of few words who kept his doors shut and held aloof from public life.

sentences.zh: 蔣琬、費禕等皆器重之。

translations.literal: Jiang Wan, Fei Yi, and others all valued him heavily.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wan, Fei Yi, and their circle held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 雖學業入深，初不視天文有所論說。

translations.literal: Although learning and arts entered deep, at first he did not look at Heaven's patterns to have discourses and explanations.
translations.idiomatic: For all his learning he rarely lectured on astrology.

sentences.zh: 後近通儒譙周常問其意，瓊答曰：「欲明此術甚難，須當身視，識其形色，不可信人也。

translations.literal: Later the thorough scholar Qiao Zhou often asked his meaning; Qiong answered saying, "To clarify this art is very difficult; one must personally look and recognize its form and color— one cannot trust others.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qiao Zhou pressed him on the subject. Qiong replied, "That art is hard to teach: you must watch the sky yourself and learn the shapes— you cannot take another's word."

sentences.zh: 晨夜苦劇，然後知之，復憂漏洩，不如不知，是以不復視也。

translations.literal: Dawn and night bitterly intense, afterward one knows it; again one worries about leaking— better not to know; therefore I do not again look."
translations.idiomatic: It means sleepless nights of observation, and even then you dread letting secrets slip— ignorance may be safer, so I no longer watch the heavens."

sentences.zh: 」周因問曰：「昔周徵君以為當塗高者魏也，其義何也？

translations.literal: Zhou thereupon asked saying, "In old days the summoned gentleman Zhou thought dangtu gao meant Wei; what was the meaning?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhou pressed him: "Your father read High on the Road as Wei— what did he mean?"

sentences.zh: 」瓊答曰：「魏，闕名也，當塗而高，聖人取類而言耳。

translations.literal: Qiong answered saying, "Wei is the name of the palace gate tower; standing on the road and high— the sage took a category and spoke thus."
translations.idiomatic: Qiong said, "Wei names the palace gate; standing high on the road— the sage was speaking in riddles."

sentences.zh: 」又問周曰：「寧復有所怪邪？

translations.literal: Again he asked Zhou saying, "Is there again something strange?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhou asked again whether anything else seemed odd.

sentences.zh: 」周曰：「未達也。

translations.literal: Zhou said, "I have not understood."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou admitted he still did not see it.

sentences.zh: 」瓊又曰：「古者名官職不言曹，始自漢已來，名官盡言曹。

translations.literal: Qiong again said, "In antiquity in naming offices one did not say Cao; beginning from Han onward, in naming offices all say Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong added, "Ancient offices were not called cao; since Han every bureau is a cao.

sentences.zh: 吏言屬曹，卒言侍曹，此殆天意也。」

translations.literal: Clerks speak of belonging to cao; privates speak of attending cao— this is nearly Heaven's intent."
translations.idiomatic: Officials speak of their cao, soldiers of attending cao— that may be Heaven's own pun on the house of Cao."

sentences.zh: 瓊年八十餘，延熙十三年卒。

translations.literal: Qiong was past eighty; in the thirteenth year of Yanxi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirteenth year of Yanxi, aged over eighty.

sentences.zh: 著《韓詩章句》十餘萬言，不教諸子，內學無傳業者。

translations.literal: He authored more than ten thousand words of Han Poetry chapter-and-verse gloss; he did not instruct his sons; among inner learning there was none who transmitted his profession.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote over ten thousand characters of commentary on the Han version of the Odes but taught none of his sons; his esoteric learning died with him.

sentences.zh: 周緣瓊言，乃觸類而長之曰：

translations.literal: Zhou by Qiong's words thereupon touched categories and extended them saying,
translations.idiomatic: Taking his cue from Du Qiong, Qiao Zhou pressed the same logic further:

sentences.zh: 《春秋傳》著秦穆候名太子曰仇，弟曰成師。

translations.literal: The Zuo commentary on the Spring and Autumn records that Duke Mu of Qin named the heir apparent Chou and the younger brother Chengshi.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo tradition tells how Duke Mu of Qin named his heir Chou and his younger son Chengshi.

sentences.zh: 師服曰：『異哉君之名子也！

translations.literal: Shi Fu said, "Strange indeed is the lord's naming of sons!"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Fu exclaimed, "What strange names the duke has chosen for his sons!"

sentences.zh: 嘉耦曰妃，怨耦曰仇，今君名太子曰仇，弟曰成師，始兆亂矣，兄其替乎？

translations.literal: A happy match is called fei; a resentful match is called chou; now the lord names the heir apparent Chou and the younger brother Chengshi— the first omen of disorder has appeared; will the elder be replaced?"
translations.idiomatic: A loving match is fei; a hostile match is chou. To call the heir Chou and the younger brother Chengshi is to invite strife— will the elder lose his place?"

sentences.zh: 』其後果如服言。

translations.literal: Afterward it indeed was as Fu had said.
translations.idiomatic: Events proved Shi Fu right.

sentences.zh: 及漢靈帝名二子曰史候、董候，既立為帝，後皆免為諸侯，與師服言相似也。

translations.literal: When Han Lingdi named two sons Shi marquis and Dong marquis, after they were established as emperors, later both were demoted to feudal lords— similar to Shi Fu's words.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ling named two sons Marquis of Shi and Marquis of Dong; both briefly mounted the throne and were then reduced to common nobles— another echo of Shi Fu's warning.

sentences.zh: 先主諱備，其訓具也，後主諱禪，其訓授也，如言劉已具矣，當授與人也；

translations.literal: The First Lord's taboo name is Bei, its gloss is complete; the Later Lord's taboo name is Shan, its gloss is to hand over; as if saying Liu is already complete, ought to hand over to others;
translations.idiomatic: The First Lord's name Bei means "complete"; the Later Lord's name Shan means "to yield"— as if the house of Liu were finished and ready to pass the mandate on;

sentences.zh: 意者甚於穆候、靈帝之名子。

translations.literal: the meaning is graver than Duke Mu's and Lingdi's naming of sons.
translations.idiomatic: a darker omen than Duke Mu's or Lingdi's choice of names.

sentences.zh: 後宦人黃皓弄權於內，景耀五年，宮中大樹無故自折，周深憂之，無所與言，乃書柱曰：「眾而大，期之會，具而授，若何復？

translations.literal: Later the eunuch Huang Hao played with power within; in the fifth year of Jingyao, a great tree in the palace for no reason broke itself; Zhou deeply worried about it, having none to speak with; therefore he wrote on a pillar saying, "Many and great, the meeting of expectation; complete and to hand over— how can there again be?"
translations.idiomatic: Later, as Huang Hao meddled at court, a great tree in the palace snapped without wind in the fifth year of Jingyao. Zhou scratched a couplet on a pillar: "Many and great— the hour draws near; complete then yielded— what can rise again?"

sentences.zh: 」言曹者眾也，魏者大也，眾而大，天下其當會也，具而授，如何復有立者乎？

translations.literal: Speaking of cao means many; speaking of wei means great; many and great— the realm ought to meet; complete and to hand over— how can there again be one who stands?"
translations.idiomatic: Cao means "host of officials"; wei means "great." Many and great— the realm will unite under Wei. Complete and yielded— how could Shu stand again?"

sentences.zh: 蜀既亡，咸以周言為驗。

translations.literal: When Shu was already lost, all took Zhou's words as verified.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu fell, everyone called Zhou a prophet.

sentences.zh: 周曰：「此雖己所推尋，然有所因，由杜君之辭而廣之耳，殊無神思獨至之異也。」

translations.literal: Zhou said, "This although is what I myself pushed and sought, yet there was something it relied on— I broadened it from Lord Du's words— in the end there was no spirit thought uniquely arriving that was different."
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zhou said, "I only extended what Du Qiong had already hinted; there was no mystic flash of my own."

sentences.zh: 許慈字仁篤，南陽人也。

translations.literal: Xu Ci, courtesy name Rendu, was a man of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ci, courtesy name Rendu, came from Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 師事劉熙，善鄭氏學，治《易》、《尚書》、《三禮》、《毛詩》、《論語》。

translations.literal: He took as teacher Liu Xi, was good at the Zheng school learning, and studied the Changes, Documents, the three ritual classics, Mao Poetry, and the Analects.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Liu Xi, mastered the Zheng school tradition, and worked through the Changes, Documents, the three ritual texts, Mao's Poetry, and the Analects.

sentences.zh: 建安中，與許靖等俱自交州入蜀。

translations.literal: In the Jianan period he together with Xu Jing and others all from Jiaozhou entered Shu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianan years he crossed from Jiaozhou into Shu with Xu Jing and others.

sentences.zh: 時又有魏郡胡潛，字公興，不知其所以在益土。

translations.literal: At that time there was also Hu Qian of Wei commandery, courtesy name Gongxing, not knowing why he was on Yi soil.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Qian of Wei commandery, courtesy name Gongxing, had also turned up in Shu for reasons now unknown.

sentences.zh: 潛雖學不沾洽，然卓犖強識，祖宗制度之儀，喪紀五服之數，皆指掌畫地，舉手可採。

translations.literal: Although Qian's learning did not soak through thoroughly, yet he was outstanding and strong in memory; the rites of ancestor temples and institutions, the numbers of mourning and the five garments— all he could sketch on the ground with a finger and raise the hand to gather.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's scholarship was patchy, but his memory was prodigious: ancestral temple protocol, mourning grades, and five-garment rules— he could trace them in the dust from memory.

sentences.zh: 先主定蜀，承喪亂歷紀，學業衰廢，乃鳩合典籍，沙汰眾學。

translations.literal: When the First Lord pacified Shu, succeeding mourning chaos spanning years, learning and arts decayed and were abandoned; therefore he gathered and combined the classical collections and sifted the many scholars.
translations.idiomatic: After the First Lord conquered Shu, years of war had ruined scholarship; he gathered texts and culled the scholars.

sentences.zh: 慈、潛並為學士，與孟光、來敏等典掌舊文。

translations.literal: Ci and Qian together were erudites, together with Meng Guang, Lai Min, and others canonically grasped old texts.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ci and Hu Qian became court erudites alongside Meng Guang and Lai Min, charged with curating the classics.

sentences.zh: 值庶事草創，動多疑議，慈、潛更相剋伐，謗讟忿急，形於聲色；

translations.literal: Meeting many matters at grass beginning, movement often had doubtful debate; Ci and Qian mutually attacked and felled, slander and abuse resentful and urgent, showing in voice and countenance;
translations.idiomatic: In those rough early days every policy sparked quarrels; Ci and Qian sniped at each other with public insults and black looks;

sentences.zh: 書籍有無，不相通借，時尋楚撻，以相震攇。

translations.literal: in books and documents having or not, they did not mutually borrow through; at times they sought Chu beating, to mutually threaten and shake.
translations.idiomatic: they hoarded books from each other and sometimes squared off with rods, trying to intimidate one another.

sentences.zh: 〈攇，虛晚反。〉

translations.literal: The graph xian is read xu-wan fan.
translations.idiomatic: The character xian is glossed with the reading xu-wan.

sentences.zh: 其矜己妒彼，乃至於此。

translations.literal: Their self-conceit and jealousy of each other reached this point.
translations.idiomatic: Their vanity and mutual jealousy had sunk to such depths.

sentences.zh: 先主愍其若斯，羣僚大會，使倡家假為二子之容，效其訟鬩之狀，酒酣樂作，以為嬉戲。

translations.literal: The First Lord pitied them being thus; at a great assembly of the host of officials he had entertainers feign the two men's appearance, enacting the form of their quarrel and strife; when wine was deep and music rose, he took it as sport.
translations.idiomatic: The First Lord took pity on their feud. At a full court banquet he had actors mimic the two scholars, acting out their bickering for comic relief once the wine flowed.

sentences.zh: 初以辭義相難，終以刀杖相屈，用感切之。

translations.literal: At first with rhetoric and meaning they challenged each other; in the end with knives and staves they humbled each other— using this to move them with cutting force.
translations.idiomatic: The skit began with verbal sparring and ended in a mock brawl with props— a pointed lesson in how ugly their rivalry had become.

sentences.zh: 潛先沒，慈後主世稍遷至大長秋，卒。

translations.literal: Qian died first; Ci in the Later Lord's age was gradually transferred to grand prolonger of autumn and died.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Qian died first. Xu Ci survived into the Later Lord's reign, rose to grand prolonger of autumn, and died there.

sentences.zh: 〈孫盛曰：蜀少人士，故慈、潛等並見載述。〉

translations.literal: Sun Sheng says: Shu had few men of note; therefore Ci and Qian and others together were recorded in narrative.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng notes that Shu produced few famous scholars, which is why Xu Ci and Hu Qian earned a place in the record.

sentences.zh: 子勳傳其業，復為博士。

translations.literal: The son Xun transmitted his profession; again became erudite.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xu Xun inherited his scholarship and again held the title of court erudite.

sentences.zh: 孟光字孝裕，河南洛陽人，漢太尉孟鬱之族。

translations.literal: Meng Guang, courtesy name Xiaoyu, was a man of Luoyang in Henan, of the clan of Han grand commandant Meng Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Guang, courtesy name Xiaoyu, came from Luoyang in Henan and belonged to the line of Han grand commandant Meng Yu.

sentences.zh: 〈《續漢書》曰：鬱，中常侍孟賁之弟。〉

translations.literal: The Continued Book of Han states: Yu was younger brother of palace attendant Meng Ben.
translations.idiomatic: The Continued Han History identifies Meng Yu as the younger brother of the eunuch Meng Ben.

sentences.zh: 靈帝末為講部吏。

translations.literal: At the end of Lingdi he was clerk of the lecture section.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ling he served as a clerk in the lecture bureau.

sentences.zh: 獻帝遷都長安，遂逃人蜀，劉焉父子待以客禮。

translations.literal: When Xiandi moved the capital to Chang'an, he then fled into Shu; Liu Yan and his son treated him with guest ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor moved the court west to Chang'an, Guang fled into Shu, where Liu Yan and Liu Zhang received him as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 博物識古，無書不覽，尤銳意三史，長於漢家舊典。

translations.literal: Broad in things and knowing antiquity, without a book he did not peruse; especially he sharpened purpose on the three histories and excelled in Han house old canons.
translations.idiomatic: He was encyclopedic, read everything, and took special interest in the three histories and Han institutional precedent.

sentences.zh: 好《公羊春秋》而譏呵《左氏》，每與來敏爭此二義，光常譊譊讙咋。

translations.literal: He loved the Gongyang Spring and Autumn and ridiculed the Zuo tradition; each time with Lai Min he disputed these two meanings; Guang constantly babbled clamor and shrieked.
translations.idiomatic: He favored the Gongyang commentary and scorned the Zuo; with Lai Min he argued the point endlessly, shouting himself hoarse.

sentences.zh: 〈譊音奴交反。

translations.literal: The graph nao is read nu-jiao fan.
translations.idiomatic: The character nao is glossed nu-jiao.

sentences.zh: 讙音休袁反。

translations.literal: The graph huan is read xiu-yuan fan.
translations.idiomatic: The character huan is glossed xiu-yuan.

sentences.zh: 咋音徂格反。〉

translations.literal: The graph zha is read zu-ge fan.
translations.idiomatic: The character zha is glossed zu-ge.

sentences.zh: 先主定益州，拜為儀郎，與許慈等並掌制度。

translations.literal: When the First Lord pacified Yi Province, he appointed him master of ceremonies, together with Xu Ci and others jointly grasping institutions.
translations.idiomatic: After the First Lord took Yi Province he named Guang master of ceremonies alongside Xu Ci to codify court ritual.

sentences.zh: 後主踐阼，為符節令、屯騎校尉、長樂少府，遷大司農。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord ascended the throne, he became marshal of credentials, colonel of the agile cavalry, junior steward of Chang-le, transferred to grand minister of agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Later Lord he rose from marshal of credentials and colonel of the agile cavalry to junior steward of Changle palace and finally grand minister of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 延熙九年秋，大赦，光於眾中責大將軍費禕曰：「夫赦者，偏枯之物，非明世所宜有也。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the ninth year of Yanxi there was a great amnesty; Guang in the midst of the crowd rebuked grand general Fei Yi saying, "An amnesty is a thing of one-sided withering— not what a clear age ought to have.
translations.idiomatic: When a general amnesty was proclaimed in the ninth year of Yanxi, Guang publicly scolded Fei Yi: "Mercy decrees are a crutch for failing states, not the tool of a well-ordered realm.

sentences.zh: 衰弊窮極，必不得已，然後乃可權而行之耳。

translations.literal: Decline and exhaustion reaching the utmost, only when there is no choice may one by weight carry it out."
translations.idiomatic: They belong to ages of collapse, when there is truly no alternative— only then may you resort to them."

sentences.zh: 今主上仁賢，百僚稱職，有何旦夕之危，倒懸之急，而數施非常之恩，以惠姦宄之惡乎？

translations.literal: Now the lord is humane and worthy; the hundred officials are called competent— what dawn-and-dusk peril, upside-down urgency, that you repeatedly apply extraordinary grace to benefit the wickedness of traitors?"
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign is wise, his ministers capable— what sudden peril warrants showering criminals with repeated pardons?"

sentences.zh: 又鷹隼始擊，而更原宥有罪，上犯天時，下違人理。

translations.literal: Moreover hawks and falcons have just struck, yet you again forgive and pardon the guilty— above offending Heaven's season, below violating human principle."
translations.idiomatic: Autumn is the season of the law, yet you spare felons— you offend both the calendar and common sense."

sentences.zh: 老夫耄朽，不達治體，窮謂其法難以經久，豈具瞻之高美，所望於明德哉。

translations.literal: This old man is decrepit and decayed, not comprehending the body of governance; in the end I say its method is hard to endure long— is this the lofty beauty of being gazed on from all sides, what is hoped from enlightened virtue?"
translations.idiomatic: I am an old fool out of touch with policy, yet I know this habit cannot last— is this what the world expects of enlightened rule?"

sentences.zh: 」禕但顧謝踧踖而已。

translations.literal: Yi only looked and apologized, cramped and uneasy, that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yi could only bow and mumble apologies, squirming in his seat.

sentences.zh: 光之指摘痛癢，多如是類。

translations.literal: Guang's pointing out itch and pain was mostly of this class.
translations.idiomatic: Guang's blunt rebukes were typical of his manner.

sentences.zh: 故執政重臣，心不能悅，爵位不登，每直言無所迴避，為代所嫌。

translations.literal: Therefore holding-government heavy ministers, in heart could not be pleased; noble rank did not ascend; each time straight words without any evasion— he was resented by his generation.
translations.idiomatic: The great officers of state resented him, he rose no higher in rank, and his habit of blunt truth-telling made him widely disliked.

sentences.zh: 太常廣漢鐔承、

translations.literal: Grand master of ceremonies Tan Cheng of Guanghan,
translations.idiomatic: Tan Cheng of Guanghan, grand master of ceremonies,

sentences.zh: 〈《華陽國志》曰：承字公文，歷郡守少府。〉

translations.literal: the Huayang Guo zhi states: Cheng's courtesy name was Gongwen; he passed through commandery governorship and junior steward.
translations.idiomatic: the Huayang Guo zhi gives his courtesy name as Gongwen and lists him as a former commandery governor and junior steward.

sentences.zh: 光祿勛河東裴儁等，年資皆在光後，而登據上列，處光之右，蓋以此也。

translations.literal: Minister of the household Pei Jun of Hedong and others, in years and seniority all were behind Guang, yet they ascended and occupied upper rows, standing to Guang's right— it was roughly for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the household Pei Jun of Hedong and others were junior to Guang in age and service yet ranked above him— largely because Guang had alienated the powerful.

sentences.zh: 〈傅暢《裴氏家記》曰：儁字奉先，魏尚書令潛弟也。

translations.literal: Fu Chang's Pei clan family record states: Jun's courtesy name was Fengxian; he was younger brother of Wei director of the Masters of Writing Pei Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Chang's Pei family record identifies Jun as courtesy Fengxian, younger brother of Wei director Pei Qian.

sentences.zh: 儁姊夫爲蜀中長史，儁送之，時年十餘歲，遂遭漢末大亂，不復得還。

translations.literal: Jun's brother-in-law was chief clerk in Shu; Jun escorted him; at the time he was more than ten years of age; then encountered Han end great chaos, no longer able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Jun had escorted a brother-in-law serving as chief clerk in Shu while still a boy; the wars stranded him there.

sentences.zh: 既長知名，爲蜀所推重也。

translations.literal: When grown he became known by name and was esteemed by Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He grew up in Shu, won a reputation, and became a respected figure.

sentences.zh: 子越，字令緒，爲蜀督軍。

translations.literal: The son Yue, courtesy name Lingxu, was Shu army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pei Yue, courtesy Lingxu, became an army supervisor in Shu.

sentences.zh: 蜀破，遷還洛陽，拜議郎。〉

translations.literal: When Shu was broken, he moved back to Luoyang and was appointed master of discussion.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu fell he returned to Luoyang as a master of discussion.

sentences.zh: 後進文士秘書郎郤正數從光諮訪，光問正太子所習讀性並其性情好尚，正答曰：「奉親虔恭。

translations.literal: The rising scholar confidential clerk Xi Zheng several times followed Guang to consult; Guang asked Zheng what the heir apparent habitually read in nature together with his disposition and likes; Zheng answered saying, "Serving parents reverent and respectful.
translations.idiomatic: The young secretary Xi Zheng often sought Guang's counsel. Guang asked what the heir read and what sort of man he was. Zheng answered, "He honors his parents with devotion.

sentences.zh: 夙夜匪懈，有古世子之風；

translations.literal: Dawn and night without slack, having the air of heir sons of antiquity;
translations.idiomatic: He is diligent night and day in the mold of the classical heir;

sentences.zh: 接待羣僚，舉動出於仁恕。

translations.literal: receiving and treating the host of officials, movement and action issue from benevolence and forgiveness."
translations.idiomatic: and in dealing with officials he acts from benevolence and forbearance."

sentences.zh: 」光曰：「如君所道，皆家戶所有耳；

translations.literal: Guang said, "As you, sir, describe it, these are all what every household has;"
translations.idiomatic: Guang replied, "That is the sort of praise any family could mouth;

sentences.zh: 吾今所問，欲知其權略智調何如也。

translations.literal: what I now ask is to know how his stratagem and wit and resource are."
translations.idiomatic: I want to know his strategic mind and practical judgment."

sentences.zh: 」正曰：「世子之道，在於承志竭歡，既不得妄有所施為，且智調藏於胸懷，權略應時而發，此之有無，焉可豫設也？

translations.literal: Zheng said, "The way of the heir son lies in inheriting intent and exhausting joy; since he cannot recklessly have deeds done, moreover wit and resource hide in the breast, stratagem and calculation respond to the moment and issue forth— the having or not of this, how can one set it beforehand?"
translations.idiomatic: Zheng said, "An heir's duty is to please his father and carry on his will; he cannot scheme in the open. Clever plans stay hidden until the moment calls for them— you cannot know that in advance."

sentences.zh: 」光解正慎宜，不為放談，乃曰：「吾好直言，無所迴避，每彈射利病，為世人所譏嫌。

translations.literal: Guang understood Zheng was cautious and proper, not making reckless talk; therefore said, "I love straight speech without evasion; each time I shoot out profit and harm, I am ridiculed and resented by the world.
translations.idiomatic: Guang saw that Zheng was being discreet and said, "I always speak plainly and pay for it with the world's dislike.

sentences.zh: 疑省君意亦不甚好吾言，然語有次。

translations.literal: I suspect examining your intent also is not very fond of my words, yet speech has order.
translations.idiomatic: I suspect you do not much like my tone either, yet there is a point to my order of topics.

sentences.zh: 今天下未定，智意為先，智意雖有自然，然不可力強致也。

translations.literal: Now the realm is not settled; wit and intent come first; although wit and intent have what is natural, yet one cannot force them to arrive by strength."
translations.idiomatic: The empire is still unsettled; judgment matters most, and judgment cannot be forced.

sentences.zh: 此儲君讀書，寧當效吾等竭力博識以待訪問，如博士探策講試以求爵位邪！

translations.literal: This stored lord's reading— ought he to imitate us in exhausting strength for broad knowledge to await inquiry and visit, like erudites drawing lots in lecture and examination to seek noble rank!"
translations.idiomatic: Should the heir exhaust himself cramming trivia like a student cramming for an exam to win a salary?"

sentences.zh: 當務其急者。

translations.literal: He ought to pursue what is urgent."
translations.idiomatic: He should master what is urgent."

sentences.zh: 」正深謂光言為然。

translations.literal: Zheng deeply deemed Guang's words correct.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng agreed wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 後光坐事免官，年九十餘，卒。

translations.literal: Later Guang because of affairs sat and was stripped of office; past ninety years of age, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Guang later lost his post over an incident and died in his nineties.

sentences.zh: 來敏字敬達，義陽新野人，來歙之後也。

translations.literal: Lai Min, courtesy name Jingda, a man of Xinye in Yiyang, was posterity of Lai Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Min, courtesy name Jingda, from Xinye in Yiyang, descended from Lai Xi.

sentences.zh: 父艷，為漢司空。

translations.literal: His father Yan was Han minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lai Yan had been Han minister of works.

sentences.zh: 〈華嶠《後漢書》曰：艷好學下士，開館養徒眾。

translations.literal: Hua Qiao's Later Han History states: Yan loved learning and lowered himself to knights, opening a hall and nurturing a host of disciples.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Qiao's Later Han History says Lai Yan loved books, honored scholars, and kept a school full of pupils.

sentences.zh: 少歷顯位，靈帝時位至司空。〉

translations.literal: In youth he passed through eminent posts; in Lingdi's time his position reached minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: He rose early to high office and became minister of works under Emperor Ling.

sentences.zh: 漢末大亂，敏隨姊夫奔荊州，姊夫黃琬是劉璋祖母之侄，故璋遣迎琬妻，敏遂俱與姊入蜀，常為璋賓客。

translations.literal: At Han end great chaos, Min followed his brother-in-law fleeing to Jing Province; his brother-in-law Huang Wan was Liu Zhang's grandmother's nephew; therefore Zhang sent to welcome Wan's wife; Min then together with his elder sister entered Shu, constantly being Zhang's guest retainers.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han collapsed, Min fled to Jing with his brother-in-law Huang Wan, a kinsman of Liu Zhang's grandmother. Liu Zhang summoned Wan's household west, so Min entered Shu with his sister and stayed on as Liu Zhang's client.

sentences.zh: 涉獵書籍，善《左氏春秋》，尤精於《倉》、《雅》訓詁，好是正文字。

translations.literal: He ranged through books and documents, was good at the Zuo tradition of the Spring and Autumn Annals, especially refined in the Cangjie and Erya glosses, fond of correcting graphs and characters.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely, excelled in the Zuo commentary, and specialized in the Cangjie and Erya wordbooks, loving to emend textual errors.

sentences.zh: 先主定益州，署敏典學校尉。

translations.literal: When the First Lord pacified Yi Province, he appointed Min colonel of classical schools.
translations.idiomatic: The First Lord named him colonel of classical schools after taking Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 及立太子，以為家令。

translations.literal: When they established the heir apparent, they made him household steward to the heir.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent was named, Min became his household steward.

sentences.zh: 後主踐阼，為虎賁中郎將。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord ascended the throne, he became general of the tiger garrison at the center.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Later Lord he was promoted to general of the tiger garrison at the center.

sentences.zh: 丞相亮住漢中，請為軍祭酒、輔軍將軍，坐事去職。

translations.literal: Chancellor Liang dwelt at Hanzhong, requested him as army libationer and general who assists the army; because of affairs he lost office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang, stationed at Hanzhong, made him army libationer and general who assists the army, but he later lost the post over an incident.

sentences.zh: 〈亮集有教曰：「將軍來敏對上官顯言『新人有何功德而奪我榮資與之邪？

translations.literal: In Liang's collected directives there is an instruction saying, "General Lai Min openly said to superiors, What merit have newcomers that they seize my glory and salary and give it to them?
translations.idiomatic: Among Zhuge Liang's papers is an order noting that General Lai Min had loudly demanded of his superiors, "What have these newcomers done to strip me of my honors and pay?"

sentences.zh: 諸人共憎我，何故如是』？

translations.literal: The host of men together hate me— why are things thus?"
translations.idiomatic: Everyone turns on me— why should it be so?"

sentences.zh: 敏年老狂悖，生此怨言。

translations.literal: Min is old and mad perverse, producing these resentful words."
translations.idiomatic: Min is old, unbalanced, and mutinous."

sentences.zh: 昔成都初定，議者以為來敏亂羣，先帝以新定之際，故遂含容，無所禮用。

translations.literal: In old days when Chengdu was first settled, debaters thought Lai Min threw the group into disorder; the First Emperor because of newly settled circumstances therefore then contained him, not employing him with ritual."
translations.idiomatic: When Chengdu first fell, many had called Min a disruptive influence; the First Lord had only tolerated him while the realm was new.

sentences.zh: 後劉子初選以為太子家令，先帝不悅而不忍拒也。

translations.literal: Later Liu Zichu selected him to be household steward to the heir apparent; the First Emperor was not pleased yet could not bear to refuse.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liu Ba proposed him as the heir's steward; the First Lord disliked the choice but let it stand.

sentences.zh: 後主既位，吾闇於知人，遂復擢為將軍祭酒，違議者之審見，背先帝所疏外，自謂能以敦厲薄俗，帥之以義。

translations.literal: After the Later Lord already took position, I was dark in knowing men, then again raised him as general's libationer— going against debaters' careful view, turning my back on what the First Emperor pushed aside; I myself thought I could with severity encourage thin custom and lead them with righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: When I took the throne I misjudged him and raised him again as libationer to the general— against good advice and contrary to my father's coldness toward him— thinking I could shame him into reform.

sentences.zh: 今既不能，表退職，使閉門思愆。」〉

translations.literal: Now since he cannot, memorialize stripping his post, make him close his gate and ponder faults."
translations.idiomatic: Since he will not mend his ways, strip his office and make him reflect behind closed doors."

sentences.zh: 亮卒後，還成都為大長秋，又免，後累遷為光祿大夫，復坐過黜。

translations.literal: After Liang died, he returned to Chengdu as grand prolonger of autumn; again was dismissed; later repeatedly transferred to become grand counselor of the household; again because of fault sat and was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: After Liang's death he came back to Chengdu as grand prolonger of autumn, lost that post, later rose to grand counselor of the household, and was demoted again for misconduct.

sentences.zh: 前後數貶削，皆以語言不節，舉動違常也。

translations.literal: Before and after several demotions and cuts, all were because speech lacked restraint and movement violated the norm.
translations.idiomatic: Each fall was for loose talk and erratic behavior.

sentences.zh: 時孟光亦以樞機不慎，議論干時，然猶愈於敏，俱以耆宿學士見禮於世。

translations.literal: At that time Meng Guang also because pivot and trigger were not careful, discussion and debate offended the times, yet still was better than Min; both because old-host erudites were treated with ritual by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Guang likewise offended the court with ill-timed opinions, though he was still easier to bear than Min; both were honored as senior scholars.

sentences.zh: 而敏荊楚名族，東宮舊臣，特加優待，是故廢而復起。

translations.literal: But Min was a great clan of Jing and Chu, an old minister of the eastern palace; especially they added generous treatment; therefore dismissed yet again raised.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Min belonged to a great Jing-Chu lineage and had long served the heir's household, so the court kept restoring him after each dismissal.

sentences.zh: 後以敏為執慎將軍，欲令以官重自警戒也，年九十七，景耀中卒。

translations.literal: Later they made Min general who holds caution, wishing to make him with office weight warn himself; at age ninety-seven, in Jingyao he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually named general who holds caution in hope that the title would sober him; he died in the Jingyao era at ninety-seven.

sentences.zh: 子忠，亦博覽經學，有敏風，與尚書向充等並能協贊大將軍姜維。

translations.literal: The son Zhong also ranged widely in classical learning, having Min's air, together with director of the Masters of Writing Xiang Chong and others were able jointly to assist grand general Jiang Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lai Zhong inherited his breadth of learning and, with Xiang Chong of the Masters of Writing, helped Jiang Wei as grand general.

sentences.zh: 維善之，以為參軍。

translations.literal: Wei was good with him, making him army adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Wei valued him and named him an army adviser.

sentences.zh: 尹默字思潛，梓潼涪人也。

translations.literal: Yin Mo, courtesy name Sizian, was a man of Fu in Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Mo, courtesy name Sizian, came from Fu in Zitong.

sentences.zh: 益部多貴今文而不祟章句，默知其不博。

translations.literal: In Yi Province many valued modern-text learning and did not honor chapter-and-verse; Mo knew it was not broad.
translations.idiomatic: Yi scholars favored modern-text studies and scorned philology; Mo saw how narrow that was.

sentences.zh: 乃遠遊荊州，從司馬德操、宋仲子等受古學。

translations.literal: Therefore he traveled far to Jing Province, from Sima Decao and Song Zhongzi and others receiving ancient learning.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Jing Province to study antiquity under Sima Hui, Song Zhongzi, and others.

sentences.zh: 皆通諸經史，又專精於《左氏春秋》，自劉歆條例，鄭眾、賈逵父子、陳元、方服虔注說，咸略誦述，不復按本。

translations.literal: He all penetrated the various classics and histories, and also specialized in the Zuo tradition of the Spring and Autumn Annals— from Liu Xin's regulations, Zheng Zhong and Jia Kui father and son, Chen Yuan, Fang, Fu Qian's commentary explanations— all he could recite from memory, no longer checking the original.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the classics and histories and made the Zuo commentary his specialty, committing Liu Xin's outlines and the glosses of Zheng Zhong, the Jias, Chen Yuan, Fang, and Fu Qian to memory without needing the text.

sentences.zh: 先主定益州，領牧，以為勸學從事。

translations.literal: When the First Lord pacified Yi Province and took the shepherd title, he made him adjutant for encouraging learning.
translations.idiomatic: After the First Lord took Yi Province and the shepherd's seal, he appointed Mo adjutant for encouraging learning.

sentences.zh: 及立太子，以默為僕，射以《左氏傳》授後主。

translations.literal: When they established the heir apparent, they appointed Mo as tutor and used the Zuo Tradition to instruct the Later Lord.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent was installed, Mo became his tutor and taught the Later Lord from the Zuo Tradition.

sentences.zh: 後主踐阼，拜諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord ascended the throne, he was appointed remonstrance grandee.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord named him remonstrance grandee at accession.

sentences.zh: 丞相亮住漢中，請為軍祭酒。

translations.literal: Chancellor Liang dwelt at Hanzhong, requested him as army libationer.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhuge Liang was at Hanzhong he summoned Mo as army libationer.

sentences.zh: 亮卒，還成都，拜大中大夫，卒。

translations.literal: When Liang died, he returned to Chengdu, was appointed grand palace counselor, died.
translations.idiomatic: After Liang's death he returned to Chengdu as grand palace counselor and died there.

sentences.zh: 子宗傳其業，為博士。

translations.literal: The son Zong transmitted his profession, became erudite.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yin Zong inherited his learning and became a court erudite.

sentences.zh: 〈宋仲子後在魏。

translations.literal: Song Zhongzi later was in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Song Zhongzi later ended up in Wei.

sentences.zh: 《魏略》曰：其子與魏諷謀反，伏誅。

translations.literal: The Wei summary states: His son plotted treason with Wei Feng and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei lüe records that Zhongzi's son joined Wei Feng's plot and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 魏太子答王朗書曰：「昔石厚與州吁遊，父碏知其與亂；

translations.literal: The Wei heir apparent answered Wang Lang's letter saying, "In old days Shi Hou traveled with Zhou Xu; father Que knew he would join disorder;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei crown prince once wrote Wang Lang: "Shi Hou kept company with Zhou Xu, and his father knew it meant trouble;

sentences.zh: 韓子暱田蘇，穆子知其好仁：故君子遊必有方，居必就士，誠有以也。

translations.literal: Hanzi was intimate with Tian Su; the Mu viscount knew he loved benevolence: therefore the gentleman in travel must have a direction, in dwelling must approach knights— there is truly reason for this.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzi befriended Tian Su, and Viscount Mu saw his goodness— a gentleman chooses his company with care for good reason.

sentences.zh: 嗟乎！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 宋忠無石子先識之明，老罹此禍。

translations.literal: Song Zhong lacked Shi Que's foreknowledge brightness; in old age he encountered this calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Song Zhong lacked Shi Que's foresight and paid for it in old age.

sentences.zh: 今雖欲原行滅親之誅，立純臣之節，尚可得邪！」〉

translations.literal: Now although one wishes to apply the punishment of destroying kin for conduct, to establish the integrity of a pure minister— can it still be obtained!"
translations.idiomatic: Even if one wished to execute a son to prove a father's loyalty, that purity is beyond reach now!"

sentences.zh: 譙周字允南，巴西西充國人也。

translations.literal: Qiao Zhou, courtesy name Yunnan, was a man of Xichongguo in Ba commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zhou, courtesy name Yunnan, came from Xichongguo in Ba commandery.

sentences.zh: 父

translations.literal: Father
translations.idiomatic: His father

sentences.zh: （山幷）

translations.literal: (the text records a damaged form of the personal name)
translations.idiomatic: (the manuscript preserves a garbled form of his father's name)

sentences.zh: ，字榮始，治《尚書》，兼通諸經及圖緯。

translations.literal: , courtesy name Rongshi, studied the Documents and also penetrated the classics and charts and wefts.
translations.idiomatic: , courtesy name Rongshi, specialized in the Documents and the esoteric classics and apocrypha.

sentences.zh: 州郡辟請，皆不應，州就假師友從事。

translations.literal: Province and commandery summoned and invited; all he did not answer; the province then appointed him acting adjutant for teachers and friends.
translations.idiomatic: He refused every provincial summons until the authorities named him acting adjutant for teachers and friends without his consent.

sentences.zh: 周幼孤，與母兄同居。

translations.literal: Zhou in youth was orphaned and dwelt together with mother and elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou lost his father young and lived with his mother and older brother.

sentences.zh: 既長，耽古篤學，家貧未嘗問產業，誦讀典籍，欣然獨笑，以忘寢食。

translations.literal: Already grown, he was addicted to antiquity and devoted to learning; the household was poor yet he never asked about estates; reciting and reading the classical collections, happily he alone laughed, thereby forgetting sleep and food.
translations.idiomatic: Grown to manhood he buried himself in the classics, indifferent to poverty, chuckling over his books until he forgot meals and sleep.

sentences.zh: 研精《六經》，尤善書札，頗曉天文，而不以留意；

translations.literal: He ground fine the Six Classics, especially was good at letters and notes, somewhat understood astronomy, yet did not apply mind to it;
translations.idiomatic: He absorbed the Six Classics, wrote elegant prose, and knew something of astronomy though he cared little for it;

sentences.zh: 諸子文章非心所存，不悉遍視也。

translations.literal: the various masters' writings were not what his heart stored; he did not all everywhere view them.
translations.idiomatic: and he skimmed the philosophers only when he had to.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，體貌素樸，性推誠不飾。

translations.literal: His body was eight chi in height; body appearance plain and simple; nature pushed sincerity without adornment.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight chi tall, dressed plainly, and was candid to a fault.

sentences.zh: 無造次辯論之才，然潛識內敏。

translations.literal: He lacked talent for hasty debate, yet inwardly was keen and quick.
translations.idiomatic: He was no quick debater but saw to the heart of things.

sentences.zh: 建興中，丞相亮領益州牧，命周為勸學從事。

translations.literal: In the Jianxing period, Chancellor Liang took concurrent post as shepherd of Yi Province, ordered Zhou as adjutant for encouraging learning.
translations.idiomatic: During Jianxing, while Zhuge Liang held stewardship of Yi Province, he named Zhou adjutant for encouraging learning.

sentences.zh: 〈《蜀記》曰：周初見亮，左右皆笑。

translations.literal: The Shu record states: When Zhou first saw Liang, those at left and right all laughed.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ji notes that when Qiao Zhou first met Zhuge Liang, the attendants laughed at him.

sentences.zh: 既出，有司請推笑者，亮曰：「孤尚不能忍，況左右乎！」〉

translations.literal: After he went out, the responsible officials requested to pursue the laughers; Liang said, "I alone still could not endure— how much more those at left and right!"
translations.idiomatic: Afterward officials wanted to punish the snickerers. Liang said, "If I could barely keep a straight face, how can I blame the staff?"

sentences.zh: 亮卒於敵庭，周在家聞問，即便奔赴，尋有詔書禁斷，惟周以速行得達。

translations.literal: When Liang died in the enemy court, Zhou at home heard the news and immediately rushed to go; soon there was an edict forbidding and cutting off; only Zhou by swift travel was able to reach.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang died on campaign, Zhou set out from home at once. An edict soon forbade travel for mourning, but Zhou moved so fast he arrived before the ban caught him.

sentences.zh: 大將軍蔣琬領刺史，徙為典學從事，總州之學者。

translations.literal: Grand general Jiang Wan took concurrent inspector, transferred him to be adjutant for canonical learning, summing the scholars of the province.
translations.idiomatic: Grand general Jiang Wan, as concurrent provincial inspector, moved him to adjutant for canonical learning to oversee the province's scholars.

sentences.zh: 後主立太子，以周為僕，轉家令。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord established the heir apparent, he made Zhou tutor, transferred household steward.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent was installed, Zhou became his tutor and then his household steward.

sentences.zh: 時後主頗出遊觀，增廣聲樂。

translations.literal: At that time the Later Lord quite went out roaming and viewing, increasing and enlarging sound and music.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord had begun touring the parks and expanding his musical establishments.

sentences.zh: 周上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: Zhou submitted a memorial remonstrating saying,
translations.idiomatic: Zhou therefore memorialized:

sentences.zh: 昔王莽之敗，豪傑並起，跨州據郡，欲弄神器，於是賢才智士思望所歸，未必以其勢之廣狹，惟其德之薄厚也。

translations.literal: In old days when Wang Mang was defeated, heroes rose together, straddling provinces and occupying commanderies, wishing to toy with the sacred vessel; then worthy wise knights pondered whom to attach to— not necessarily by the breadth or narrowness of their power, but only by the thinness or thickness of their virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Mang fell, warlords carved up the realm. Wise men chose their lords by moral weight, not by the size of an army.

sentences.zh: 是故於時更始、公孫述及諸有大眾者多己廣大，然莫不快情恣欲，怠於為善，遊獵飲食，不恤民物。

translations.literal: Therefore at that time Gengshi, Gongsun Shu, and the many who had great hosts were mostly already vast and great, yet none were not quick in feeling and wanton in desire, lazy in doing good, roaming and hunting, drinking and eating, not pitying the people and things.
translations.idiomatic: Gengshi, Gongsun Shu, and other large factions grew arrogant: they hunted, feasted, and ignored the people.

sentences.zh: 世祖初入河北，馮異等勸之曰：『當行人所不能為。

translations.literal: When the Founding Ancestor first entered Hebei, Feng Yi and others urged him saying, "You ought to practice what other men cannot practice."
translations.idiomatic: When Guangwu first entered Hebei, Feng Yi urged him to do what others would not— win the people by justice.

sentences.zh: 』遂務理冤獄，節儉飲食，動尊法度，故北州歌歎，聲布四遠。

translations.literal: Thereupon he devoted effort to straightening unjust prisons, being frugal in drink and food, moving in reverence of law and measure; therefore the northern province sang praise, sound spreading to the four distances.
translations.idiomatic: He cleared wrongful convictions, lived simply, and honored the law until the north sang his praises.

sentences.zh: 於是鄧禹自南陽追之，吳漢、寇恂未識世祖，遙聞德行，遂以權計舉漁陽、上谷突騎迎於廣阿。

translations.literal: Thereupon Deng Yu from Nanyang pursued him; Wu Han and Kou Xun did not yet know the Founding Ancestor; from afar hearing conduct and virtue, then by stratagem raised Fuyang and Shanggu shock cavalry to welcome him at Guang'e.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yu rode from Nanyang to join him; Wu Han and Kou Xun, though they had never met him, sent the crack cavalry of Fuyang and Shanggu to meet him at Guang'e on the strength of his reputation.

sentences.zh: 其望風慕德者邳肜、耿純、劉植之徒，至於輿病繼棺，繈負而至者，不可勝數，故能以弱為強，屠王郎，吞銅馬，折赤眉而成帝業也。

translations.literal: Those who looked to the wind and admired virtue, Pi Tong, Geng Chun, Liu Zhi and their class, reaching those who in carts carried illness and linked coffins, or in swaddling were borne and arrived— could not be counted; therefore he was able with the weak to be strong, slaughter Wang Lang, swallow the Bronze Horses, break the Red Eyebrows and complete the imperial enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Pi Tong and Geng Chun flocked to him— some carried on sickbeds, others brought infants— too many to count. Thus he turned weakness into strength, destroyed Wang Lang, absorbed the Bronze Horse bands, crushed the Red Eyebrows, and founded the Eastern Han.

sentences.zh: 及在洛陽，嘗欲小出，車駕已御，銚期諫曰：『天下未寧，臣誠不願陛下細行數出。

translations.literal: When at Luoyang he once wished to go out a little; the carriage team was already yoked; Yao Qi remonstrated saying, "The realm is not yet tranquil; your servant truly does not wish Your Majesty to go out often on small trips."
translations.idiomatic: Even at Luoyang, when he once ordered a minor outing, Yao Qi warned him, "The realm is still unsettled; please do not ride out on whim."

sentences.zh: 』即時還車。

translations.literal: Immediately he returned the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: He turned the chariot back at once.

sentences.zh: 及征隗囂，穎川盜起，世祖還洛陽，但遣寇恂往，恂曰：『穎川以陛下遠征，故奸猾起叛，未知陛下還，恐不時降；

translations.literal: When campaigning against Wei Ao, in Yingchuan bandits arose; the Founding Ancestor returned to Luoyang, only sent Kou Xun to go; Xun said, "Yingchuan because Your Majesty marched far on campaign, therefore the crafty and slippery rose in rebellion; not knowing Your Majesty has returned, I fear they will not submit in time;
translations.idiomatic: During the Wei Ao campaign, Yingchuan rebelled. Guangwu stayed in Luoyang and sent only Kou Xun, who said, "The rebels think you are still far away; they will not yield until they know you have returned;

sentences.zh: 陛下自臨，穎川賊必即降。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty personally comes, the Yingchuan bandits will certainly immediately submit."
translations.idiomatic: but if you appear in person, they will collapse at once."

sentences.zh: 』遂至穎川，竟如恂言。

translations.literal: Thereupon he reached Yingchuan; in the end it was as Xun had said.
translations.idiomatic: He rode south and it happened exactly as Kou Xun predicted.

sentences.zh: 故非急務，欲小出不敢，至於急務，欲自安不為，故帝者之欲善也如此！

translations.literal: Therefore when it was not urgent business, wishing to go out a little he did not dare; reaching urgent business, wishing to secure himself he did not do it— therefore the emperor's desire for good was thus!
translations.idiomatic: He would not stir for pleasure, yet never shirked duty— such was an emperor's discipline.

sentences.zh: 故《傳》曰『百姓不徒附』，誠以德先之也。

translations.literal: Therefore the tradition says "the hundred surnames do not vainly attach"— truly because virtue leads them first.
translations.idiomatic: The classic line runs, "The people do not rally without reason"— they follow virtue first.

sentences.zh: 今漢遭厄運，天下三分，雄哲之士思望之時也。

translations.literal: Now Han has encountered ill fortune; the realm is three-divided; it is the time when heroic wise men ponder whom to attach to.
translations.idiomatic: Han is broken into three; this is the hour when heroes choose their lord.

sentences.zh: 陛下天姿至孝，喪逾三年，言及隕涕，雖曾、閔不過也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's Heaven-endowment is utmost filial; mourning passed three years; speaking of it you fall tears— though Zeng and Min could not surpass it.
translations.idiomatic: Your filial mourning for the late emperor exceeded three years and moved all who heard you— Zengzi and Min Sun could have done no more.

sentences.zh: 敬賢任才，使之盡力，有逾成、康。

translations.literal: Respecting worthies and appointing talent, causing them to exhaust strength, has surpassed Cheng and Kang.
translations.idiomatic: You honor the worthy and employ talent to the full— a standard beyond even the kings Cheng and Kang.

sentences.zh: 故國內和一，大小戮力，臣所不能陳。

translations.literal: Therefore within the state harmony is one; great and small join strength— what your servant cannot set forth.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is united and every rank pulls together— more than words can say.

sentences.zh: 然臣不勝大願，願復廣人所不能者。

translations.literal: Yet your servant cannot overcome a great wish; I wish again to broaden what people cannot do.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I beg you to attempt what common men find hardest.

sentences.zh: 夫挽大重者，其用力苦不眾，拔大艱者，其善術苦不廣，且承事宗廟者，非徒求福祐，所以率民尊上也。

translations.literal: For dragging a great heavy thing, if the force used is not many it is bitter; for uprooting a great hardship, if the good art is not broad it is bitter; moreover those who undertake service to the ancestral temples do not only seek blessing and protection— it is the means to lead the people in revering the superior.
translations.idiomatic: Great burdens need many hands; grave crises need broad counsel. Tending the shrines is not mere ritual— it teaches the people to revere their ruler.

sentences.zh: 至於四時之祀，或有不臨，池苑之觀；

translations.literal: As for the four seasons' sacrifices, sometimes there is not personal attendance; the pools and parks for viewing;
translations.idiomatic: Yet seasonal rites are sometimes missed for pleasure trips to pools and parks;

sentences.zh: 或有仍出，臣之愚滯，私不自安。

translations.literal: sometimes there is still going out— your servant's foolish dullness, privately is not self at peace.
translations.idiomatic: and the court still rides out for sport— this dull subject cannot rest easy.

sentences.zh: 夫憂責在身者，不暇盡樂，先帝之志，堂構未成，誠非盡樂之時。

translations.literal: For one who bears care and responsibility on his person, there is no leisure to exhaust joy; the First Emperor's intent, the hall frame not yet completed— truly this is not the time to exhaust joy.
translations.idiomatic: A man with the weight of the realm on his shoulders cannot indulge every whim. Your father's work is unfinished— this is no season for revelry.

sentences.zh: 願省減樂官、後宮所增造，但奉備先帝所施，下為子孫節儉之教。

translations.literal: I wish you would examine and reduce the music officials and rear palace additions, only reverently prepare what the First Emperor established, below giving to sons and grandsons a teaching of frugality.
translations.idiomatic: Cut the music bureau and harem expansions, keep only what the late emperor ordained, and leave your heirs an example of thrift.

sentences.zh: 徙為中散大夫，猶侍太子。

translations.literal: He was transferred to grand master of scattered rank, still attending the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted to grand master of scattered rank while remaining tutor to the heir.

sentences.zh: 於時軍旅數出，百姓凋瘁，周與尚書令陳祗論其利害，退而書之，謂之《仇國論》，其辭曰：

translations.literal: At that time the army and host repeatedly went out; the hundred surnames were withered and wasted; Zhou with director of the Masters of Writing Chen Zhi discussed their profit and harm; retiring he wrote it, calling it the Discourse on Enemy States; its words say,
translations.idiomatic: Constant campaigning had exhausted the people. Zhou debated policy with Chen Zhi, director of the Masters of Writing, then wrote the Discourse on Enemy States. It begins:

sentences.zh: 因餘之國小，而肇建之國大，並爭於世而為仇敵。

translations.literal: The state of Remainder was small, while the state Founded Anew was large; together they strove in the age and became enemy foes.
translations.idiomatic: Imagine a small survivor state and a large new power locked in rivalry.

sentences.zh: 因餘之國有高賢卿者，問於伏愚子曰：「今國事未定，上下勞心，往古之事，能以弱勝強者，其術何如？

translations.literal: The state Remainder had a high worthy minister who asked the Hermit Fuyuzi saying, "Now state affairs are not settled; above and below labor in heart; in matters of past ages, those able with the weak to overcome the strong— what was their art?"
translations.idiomatic: A worthy minister of the lesser state asks a recluse: "In unstable times, how did the weak ever defeat the strong?"

sentences.zh: 」伏愚子曰：「吾聞之，處大無患者恆多慢，處小有憂者恆思善；

translations.literal: The Hermit Fuyuzi said, "I have heard: those who dwell in greatness without calamity always are much negligent; those who dwell in smallness with worry always think of good;
translations.idiomatic: The recluse answers: "Great powers grow careless; small ones stay vigilant;

sentences.zh: 多慢則生亂，恩善則生治，理之常也。

translations.literal: much negligence then produces disorder; thinking good then produces order— this is the constant of pattern."
translations.idiomatic: carelessness breeds chaos, vigilance order— that is the rule of things."

sentences.zh: 故周文養民，以少取多；

translations.literal: Therefore King Wen nurtured the people and with the few took the many;
translations.idiomatic: King Wen nourished his people and won many with few;

sentences.zh: 勾踐卹眾，以弱斃強，此其術也。

translations.literal: Goujian pitied the masses and with the weak brought death to the strong— this is their art."
translations.idiomatic: Goujian cherished his troops and destroyed a stronger foe— that is the art."

sentences.zh: 」賢卿曰：「囊者項強漢弱，相與戰爭，無日寧息，然項羽與漢約分鴻溝為界，各欲歸息民；

translations.literal: The worthy minister said, "In the past Xiang was strong and Han weak; mutually they waged war without a day of peace; yet Xiang Yu covenanted with Han to divide at Hong Canal as boundary, each wishing to return and rest the people;
translations.idiomatic: The minister objects: "Xiang Yu was strong, Han weak, yet they agreed at the Hong Canal to rest their peoples;

sentences.zh: 張良以為民志既定，則難動也，尋帥追羽，終斃項氏，豈必由文王之事乎？

translations.literal: Zhang Liang thought the people's will already settled, then hard to move; soon he led pursuit of Yu and in the end brought death to the Xiang clan— did it have to follow King Wen's affair?"
translations.idiomatic: but Zhang Liang argued that popular sentiment, once fixed, could not be stirred again; he drove the pursuit that finished Xiang Yu— need that imitate King Wen's slow virtue?"

sentences.zh: 肇建之國方有疾疢，我因其隙，陷其邊陲，覬增其疾而斃之也。

translations.literal: The state Founded Anew just had sickness; I by its crack invade its border marches, hoping to increase its sickness and bring it to death."
translations.idiomatic: The new state is already ill; strike its borders and widen the crack until it dies."

sentences.zh: 」伏愚子曰：「當殷、周之際，王候世尊，君臣久固，民習所專；

translations.literal: The Hermit Fuyuzi said, "At the Yin and Zhou transition, kings and marquises were exalted in the world; ruler and minister long were firm; the people practiced what they specialized in;
translations.idiomatic: The recluse replies: "At the Yin-Zhou transition lords had ruled for generations; customs were fixed;

sentences.zh: 深根者難拔，據固者難遷。

translations.literal: deep-rooted ones are hard to uproot; those who occupy firmness are hard to shift."
translations.idiomatic: deep roots resist uprooting and strongholds do not shift easily."

sentences.zh: 當此之時，雖漢祖安能杖劍鞭馬而取天下乎？

translations.literal: At this time, even Han's ancestor how could he grasp sword and whip horse to take the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: In such an age not even Han Gaozu could have seized the realm by sword alone."

sentences.zh: 當秦罷候置守之後，民疲秦役，天下土崩；

translations.literal: When Qin abolished marquises and set guardians afterward, the people were weary of Qin corvee; the realm was earth-broken;
translations.idiomatic: After Qin replaced feudal lords with magistrates, the people collapsed under corvee;

sentences.zh: 或歲改主，或月易公，鳥驚獸駭，莫知所從，於是豪強並爭，虎裂狼分，疾搏者獲多，遲後者見吞。

translations.literal: some years changed lord, some months changed duke; birds startled and beasts frightened, none knew what to follow from; then the powerful rose together, tigers tore and wolves divided— the swift in striking obtained much, the late in coming were seen swallowed.
translations.idiomatic: lords changed yearly, magistrates monthly; the realm panicked; strongmen tore it apart and the bold devoured the slow.

sentences.zh: 今我與肇建皆傳國易世矣，既非秦末鼎沸之時，實有六國並據之勢，故可為文王，難為漢祖。

translations.literal: Now I and Founded Anew both have transmitted the state and changed generations; it is already not the time of Qin end cauldron boiling, but truly has the situation of the six states side by side holding— therefore one can be King Wen, hard to be Han's ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Today we and Wei are both mature states, not the boiling chaos of Qin's end nor a simple duel of two powers— we may still play King Wen's patient game, but we cannot replay Han Gaozu's gambit."

sentences.zh: 夫民疲勞，則騷擾之兆生，上慢下暴則瓦解之形起。

translations.literal: When the people are weary and fatigued, then omens of disturbance arise; when superiors are negligent and inferiors violent, then the form of tile dissolution arises.
translations.idiomatic: When the people tire, rebellion stirs; when rulers grow arrogant and subjects harsh, the state cracks.

sentences.zh: 諺曰：『射幸數跌，不如審發。
