translations.literal: The proverb says, "In shooting, lucky hits often stumble— better to aim carefully and loose."
translations.idiomatic: The proverb says, "Many hasty shots miss; one careful arrow hits."

sentences.zh: 』是故智者不為小利移目，不為意似改步，時可而後動，數合而後舉，故湯、武之師不再戰而克，誠重民勞而度時審也。

translations.literal: Therefore the wise do not for small profit shift the eye, do not for seeming intention change step; when the time permits then afterward move, when the count fits then afterward raise— therefore Tang and Wu's hosts did not fight twice yet conquered; truly they valued the people's labor and measured the time carefully."
translations.idiomatic: The wise ignore small bait and false openings; they strike when heaven and numbers align— hence Tang and Wu won without repeated battles, because they weighed the people's strength and the season."

sentences.zh: 如遂極武黜征，土崩勢生，不幸遇難，雖有智者將不能謀之矣；

translations.literal: If one then exhausts martial might and dismisses campaigns, earth-broken momentum arises; if unluckily meeting disaster, though there be a wise man he will not be able to plan for it;
translations.idiomatic: If you wage total war heedlessly, the realm crumbles; when disaster strikes, no wit can save you;

sentences.zh: 若乃奇變縱橫，出入無間，沖波截轍，超谷越山，不由舟楫而濟盟津者，我愚子也，實所不及。」

translations.literal: if then strange shifts run criss-cross, going out and entering without gap, dashing waves and cutting wheel-tracks, leaping valleys and crossing mountains, without using boats and oars yet crossing the alliance ford— I am a foolish child and truly cannot reach this."
translations.idiomatic: and if you expect miracles— secret marches over mountains without fleets crossing the Yellow River— I am too dull for such schemes."

sentences.zh: 後遷光祿大夫，位亞九列。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to grand counselor of the household, rank second to the nine columns.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to grand counselor of the household, just below the nine ministers.

sentences.zh: 周雖不與政事，以儒行見禮。

translations.literal: Although Zhou did not join government affairs, by Confucian conduct he was treated with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Though he held no executive power, the court honored him as a Confucian elder.

sentences.zh: 時訪大議，輒據經以對，而後生好事者亦諮問所疑焉。

translations.literal: When they consulted great debate, he always relied on the classics to answer; and rising youths fond of affairs also consulted what they doubted.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever great policy was debated, he answered from the classics, and younger scholars brought him their questions.

sentences.zh: 景耀六年冬，魏大將軍鄧艾克江由，長驅而前。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixth year of Jingyao, Wei grand general Deng Ai took Jiangyou and drove long forward.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Jingyao 6, Wei's Deng Ai broke through Jiangyou and raced inward.

sentences.zh: 而蜀本謂敵不便至，不作城守調度。

translations.literal: Yet Shu originally thought the enemy would not conveniently arrive, and did not make city defense arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: Shu had assumed the foe would not penetrate so fast and had left the passes undefended.

sentences.zh: 及聞艾已人陰平，百姓擾擾，皆進山野，不可禁制。

translations.literal: When they heard Ai had already entered Yinping, the hundred surnames were disturbed and all advanced into mountain and wild, unable to be forbidden and controlled.
translations.idiomatic: When word spread that Deng Ai had crossed into Yinping, the populace panicked and fled to the hills beyond control.

sentences.zh: 後主使臣羣會議，計無所出。

translations.literal: The Later Lord sent ministers to a group meeting; plans came out from nowhere.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord convened his ministers; no one had a plan.

sentences.zh: 或以為蜀之與吳，本為和國，宜可奔吳；

translations.literal: Some thought Shu's relation with Wu was originally a friendly state and ought to be able to flee to Wu;
translations.idiomatic: Some urged flight to Wu as a fellow state against Wei;

sentences.zh: 或以為南中七郡，阻險鬥絕，易以自守，宜可奔南。

translations.literal: some thought the seven southern commanderies, blocked by peril and cut off by struggle, were easy to self-defend in and ought to be able to flee south.
translations.idiomatic: others argued for the seven southern commanderies, rugged and remote, as a defensible refuge.

sentences.zh: 惟周以為：

translations.literal: Only Zhou thought,
translations.idiomatic: Only Qiao Zhou argued that,

sentences.zh: 自古以來，無寄他國為天子者也，今若入吳，固當臣服。

translations.literal: From antiquity onward there has never been one who lodged in another state as Son of Heaven; now if we enter Wu, solidly we ought to submit as ministers.
translations.idiomatic: no Son of Heaven has ever ruled from a neighbor's court; if we flee to Wu we must bow to Sun Wu.

sentences.zh: 且政理不殊，則大能吞小，此數之自然也。

translations.literal: Moreover where government order is not different, the great can swallow the small— this is the naturalness of numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Where institutions are alike, the larger power devours the smaller— that is arithmetic.

sentences.zh: 由此言之，則魏能並吳，吳不能並魏明矣。

translations.literal: From this speaking, then Wei can annex Wu; Wu cannot annex Wei— it is clear.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Wei can absorb Wu, but Wu can never absorb Wei.

sentences.zh: 等為小稱臣，孰與為大？

translations.literal: Equal in being small and calling ourselves ministers— how does it compare with being great?
translations.idiomatic: Better to yield once to the greater power than twice to the lesser.

sentences.zh: 再辱之恥，何與一辱？

translations.literal: The shame of twice insult— how does it compare with one insult?
translations.idiomatic: Why suffer the double humiliation of vassalage to Wu and then to Wei?

sentences.zh: 且若欲奔南，則當早為之計，然後可果；

translations.literal: Moreover if you wish to flee south, then you ought early to have made plans for it, afterward then can it succeed;
translations.idiomatic: Flight south needed long preparation to succeed;

sentences.zh: 今大敵以近，禍敗將及，羣小之心，無一可保，恐發足之日，其變不測，何至南之有乎！

translations.literal: now the great enemy is near; disaster and defeat are about to arrive; the hearts of the petty host— none can be guaranteed; I fear the day you set foot forth, its changes cannot be fathomed— what is the point of reaching south!"
translations.idiomatic: now the enemy is at the gate and small men are unreliable— the moment you march south mutiny may break out. Why bother with the south at all?"

sentences.zh: 羣臣或難周曰：「今艾以不遠，恐不受降，如之何？

translations.literal: The host of ministers some challenged Zhou saying, "Now Ai is not far— I fear he will not accept surrender— what then?"
translations.idiomatic: Some objected: "Deng Ai is close; will he even accept our surrender?"

sentences.zh: 」周曰：「方今東吳未賓，事勢不得不受之，受之後，不得不禮。

translations.literal: Zhou said, "At present eastern Wu has not submitted; the situation of affairs forces them to accept it; after accepting, they cannot fail to treat with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou answered, "Wu is still independent, so Wei must take our surrender to win prestige; having taken it, they must treat us with face.

sentences.zh: 若陛下降魏，魏不裂土以封陛下者，周請身詣京都，以古義爭之。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty submits to Wei, if Wei does not split soil to enfeoff Your Majesty, Zhou requests personally to go to the capital and by ancient righteousness dispute it."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty yields to Wei and they refuse you a fief, I will go to Luoyang myself and argue from the classics for your due."

sentences.zh: 」眾人無以易周之理。

translations.literal: The crowd had no means to change Zhou's pattern.
translations.idiomatic: No one could refute him.

sentences.zh: 後主猶疑於入南，周上疏曰：

translations.literal: The Later Lord still hesitated about entering south; Zhou submitted a memorial saying,
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign still wavered toward the south, so Zhou wrote again:

sentences.zh: 或說陛下以北兵深入，有欲適南之計，臣愚以為不安。

translations.literal: Some have told Your Majesty that because northern troops penetrate deeply, there is a plan wishing to go south— your servant foolishly thinks it unsafe.
translations.idiomatic: Some say the northern advance makes the south the only refuge; I believe that path is perilous.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 南方遠夷之地，平常無所供為，猶數反叛，自丞相亮南征，兵勢逼之，窮乃幸從，是後供出官賦，取以給兵，以為愁怨，此患國之人也。

translations.literal: The south is the land of far barbarians; in ordinary times it supplies nothing, yet repeatedly rebels; from Chancellor Liang's southern campaign, military power pressed them; in extremity they then luckily followed; afterward they supplied outgoing official taxes, taking to supply the army— they took it as sorrow and resentment— these are people who resent the state.
translations.idiomatic: The south is wild country that even in peace pays little tax and often revolts. Zhuge Liang's expedition forced it to obey, and ever since it has groaned under levies for our armies— those peoples nurse a grudge against Shu.

sentences.zh: 今以窮迫，欲往依恃，恐必復反叛，一也；

translations.literal: Now with extremity pressed, wishing to go rely on them— I fear they will certainly again rebel— that is one;
translations.idiomatic: First, they will likely rebel if we lean on them in crisis;

sentences.zh: 北兵之來，非但取蜀而已，若奔南方，必因人勢衰，及時赴追，二也；

translations.literal: northern troops' coming is not only to take Shu; if you flee south, they must follow men's momentum in decline and in time pursue and catch— that is two;
translations.idiomatic: second, Wei did not march only against us; if we flee south they will follow our weakness and overtake us;

sentences.zh: 若至南方，外當拒敵，內供服御，費用張廣，他無所取，耗損諸夷必甚，甚必速叛，三也；

translations.literal: if you reach the south, outward you must resist the enemy, inward supply clothing and chariot— expenses spread wide; elsewhere there is nothing to take; exhausting and injuring the various barbarians must be extreme; extreme then they will quickly rebel— that is three;
translations.idiomatic: third, a southern court would face Wei abroad and feed our court at home until the tribes broke under the strain and revolted;

sentences.zh: 昔王郎以邯鄲僭號，時世祖在信都，畏逼於郎，欲棄還關中。

translations.literal: In old days Wang Lang by Handan usurped title; at that time the Founding Ancestor was at Xindu, pressed by Lang, wished to abandon and return to Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: fourth, when Wang Lang seized Handan, Guangwu in Xindu nearly fled to Guanzhong;

sentences.zh: 邳肜諫曰：『明公西還，則邯鄲城民不肯捐父母，背城主，而千里送公，其亡叛可必也。

translations.literal: Pi Tong remonstrated saying, "If the enlightened duke returns west, then Handan city people will not be willing to cast aside parents, betray the city lord, and escort the duke a thousand li— their fleeing and rebelling can be certain."
translations.idiomatic: Pi Tong warned that a western retreat would make the people of Handan abandon their lord— sure mutiny.

sentences.zh: 』世祖從之，遂破邯鄲。

translations.literal: The Founding Ancestor followed him; thereupon broke Handan.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu listened and broke Wang Lang.

sentences.zh: 今北兵至，陛下南行，誠恐邳肜之言覆信於今，四也。

translations.literal: Now when northern troops arrive, if Your Majesty goes south, I truly fear Pi Tong's words will repeat and be believed today— that is four.
translations.idiomatic: If you run south today, Pi Tong's warning will come true again— that is my fourth point.

sentences.zh: 願陛下早為之圖，可獲爵土；

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty early to make plans for it— you can obtain noble rank and soil;
translations.idiomatic: Yield now and you may still win a title and lands;

sentences.zh: 若遂適南，勢窮乃服，其禍必深。

translations.literal: if then you go south, when power is exhausted then submit, the calamity must be deep.
translations.idiomatic: delay until ruin forces surrender and your fate will be far worse.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：『亢之為言，知而不知喪，知存而不知亡；

translations.literal: The Changes says, "Excess's speaking is knowing yet not knowing loss, knowing preservation yet not knowing perishing;
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says of the top line, "Proud height means knowing gain but not loss, life but not death;

sentences.zh: 知得失存亡而不失其正者，其惟聖人乎！

translations.literal: knowing gain and loss, preservation and perishing, yet not losing correctness— is it not only the sage!"
translations.idiomatic: knowing both fortune and ruin yet holding the mean— that is the sage alone."

sentences.zh: 」言聖人知命而不苟必也，故堯，舜以子不善，知天有授，而求授人；

translations.literal: It means the sage knows fate and does not recklessly insist; therefore Yao and Shun, because sons were not good, knew Heaven had a grant and therefore sought to grant others;
translations.idiomatic: Sages accept heaven's mandate: Yao and Shun, seeing unworthy sons, sought worthier heirs;

sentences.zh: 子雖不肖，禍尚未萌，而迎綬於人，況禍以至乎！

translations.literal: though sons were not worthy, calamity had not yet sprouted, yet they welcomed the seal from others— how much more when calamity has already arrived!"
translations.idiomatic: they yielded before disaster struck— how much more should we when disaster is at the door!"

sentences.zh: 故微子以殷王之昆，面縛銜璧而歸武王，豈所樂哉，不得已也。

translations.literal: Therefore Weizi, as Yin king's kin, with face bound and jade in mouth returned to King Wu— how could it be joy? It was having no choice.
translations.idiomatic: Weizi bound himself and offered the jade to King Wu of Zhou not from joy but from necessity.

sentences.zh: 於是遂從周策。

translations.literal: Thereupon they followed Zhou's plan.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted Qiao Zhou's counsel.

sentences.zh: 劉氏無虞，一邦蒙賴，周之謀也。

translations.literal: The Liu house had no misfortune; one state received reliance— it was Zhou's plan.
translations.idiomatic: The Liu clan survived unharmed and the state was spared— thanks to Zhou's plan.

sentences.zh: 〈孫綽評曰：譙周說後主降魏，可乎？

translations.literal: Sun Chuo's appraisal says: Qiao Zhou persuaded the Later Lord to submit to Wei— can it be right?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chuo asks whether Qiao Zhou was right to urge surrender to Wei.

sentences.zh: 曰：自為天子而乞降請命，何恥之深乎！

translations.literal: It says: Being oneself Son of Heaven yet begging surrender and requesting mandate— how deep the shame!
translations.idiomatic: He answers: For a reigning emperor to beg for his life— what deeper shame?

sentences.zh: 夫為社稷死則死之，為社稷亡則亡之。

translations.literal: For the altars of soil and grain one dies then dies; for the altars of soil and grain one perishes then perishes.
translations.idiomatic: One should die for the altars or perish with them.

sentences.zh: 先君正魏之篡，不與同天矣。

translations.literal: The First Lord corrected Wei's usurpation— he did not share Heaven with it.
translations.idiomatic: The First Lord denounced Wei's theft of the mandate and refused to share the sky with Cao Pi.

sentences.zh: 推過於其父，俛首而事讎，可謂苟存，豈大居正之道哉！

translations.literal: Shifting blame onto his father, bowing head to serve an enemy— can be called barely surviving; how is it the great way of holding correctness!
translations.idiomatic: To blame one's father and serve the foe is mere clinging to life, not the righteous path.

sentences.zh: 孫盛曰：春秋之義，國君死社稷，卿大夫死位，況稱天子而可辱於人乎！

translations.literal: Sun Sheng says: By the Spring and Autumn's meaning, the state lord dies for the altars of soil and grain, ministers and grandees die for office— how much more one who is called Son of Heaven yet can be insulted by others!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng adds that the Spring and Autumn canon expects rulers to die for the state— how can a Son of Heaven endure humiliation?

sentences.zh: 周謂萬乘之君偷生苟免，亡禮希利，要冀微榮，惑矣。

translations.literal: Zhou said the lord of ten thousand chariots stole life and barely escaped, losing ritual and hoping for profit, seeking trifling glory— he was deluded.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng concludes that Qiao Zhou urged a ruler of ten thousand chariots to cling to life without honor, chasing petty advantage— a deluded course.

sentences.zh: 且以事勢言之，理有未盡。

translations.literal: Moreover judging by the trend of affairs, in principle there are points not exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Even on pragmatic grounds, Sun Sheng's argument does not cover every case.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 禪雖庸主，實無桀、紂之酷，戰雖屢北，未有土崩之亂，縱不能君臣固守，背城借一，自可退次東鄙以思後圖。

translations.literal: Shan although was a mediocre lord, truly had no Jie or Zhou cruelty; although in war repeatedly defeated in the north, there was not yet earth-collapse disorder; even if ruler and ministers could not firmly hold the city and stake all on one battle, naturally he could have withdrawn to the eastern border to plan afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shan was a middling sovereign, not a monster like Jie or Zhou; though often defeated, his realm had not dissolved. Even if he could not hold Chengdu, he might have fallen back to the eastern garrisons and plotted recovery.

sentences.zh: 是時羅憲以重兵據白帝，霍弋以強卒鎮夜郎。

translations.literal: At that time Luo Xian with heavy troops held Baidi; Huo Yi with strong soldiers garrisoned Yelang.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Xian still held Baidi with a strong force; Huo Yi still commanded Yelang.

sentences.zh: 蜀土險狹，山水峻隔，絕巘激湍，非步卒所涉。

translations.literal: Shu soil is perilous and narrow; mountains and waters steeply block; sheer cliffs and racing torrents— not what foot soldiers can cross.
translations.idiomatic: Shu is a maze of cliffs and rapids that infantry cannot easily cross.

sentences.zh: 若悉取舟楫，保據江州，徵兵南中，乞師東國，如此則姜、廖五將自然雲從，吳之三師承命電赴，何投寄之無所而慮於必亡邪？

translations.literal: If you gather all boats and oars, secure and occupy Jiangzhou, levy troops in the southern interior, beg an army from the eastern state— thus then Jiang, Liao, and the five generals naturally will cloud-follow; Wu's three hosts will accept orders and lightning hasten— what casting about with nowhere to lodge and worrying over certain destruction!
translations.idiomatic: Seize the river fleet, fortify Jiangzhou, call up the southern tribes, and beg an expedition from Wu— then generals such as Jiang Wei would rally, Wu's armies would answer the call, and you would hardly be homeless wanderers awaiting doom.

sentences.zh: 魏師之來，褰國大舉，欲追則舟楫靡資，欲留則師老多虞。

translations.literal: When Wei hosts come, raising the state in great undertaking— if they wish to pursue then boats and oars lack resources; if they wish to stay then the army ages and many worries arise.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's invasion strained the whole empire: to advance they lacked boats; to stay they risked a stalemate.

sentences.zh: 且屈伸有會，情勢代起，徐因思奮之民，以攻驕惰之卒，此越王所以敗闔閭，田單所以摧騎劫也，何為匆匆遽自囚虜，下堅壁於敵人，致斫石之至恨哉？

translations.literal: Moreover bending and stretching have their meetings; feeling and momentum rise in turn; slowly using people who ponder and rouse to attack arrogant lazy soldiers— this is how the Yue king defeated Helü, how Tian Dan crushed Qi Jie— why hastily hastily bind yourself captive, lay a hard wall for the enemy, and incur the utmost hatred of hacking stone!
translations.idiomatic: Fortunes turn: rouse a desperate people against weary invaders, as Goujian beat Helü or Tian Dan broke Yan— why rush to surrender and hand the enemy a propaganda victory?

sentences.zh: 葛生有云：「事之不濟則已耳，安能復為之下！

translations.literal: The Ge ballad has a saying, "If the affair does not succeed, then let it be— how can I again serve beneath them!"
translations.idiomatic: The old song says, "If we fail, so be it— I will not live as their underling."

sentences.zh: 」壯哉斯言，可以立懦夫之志矣。

translations.literal: Grand are these words— they can establish the resolve of a coward.
translations.idiomatic: Brave words— enough to stiffen a coward's spine.

sentences.zh: 觀古燕、齊、荊、越之敗，或國覆主滅，或魚縣鳥竄，終能建功立事，康復社稷，豈曰天助，抑亦人謀也。

translations.literal: Looking at the defeats of old Yan, Qi, Jing, and Yue— some states overturned and lords perished, or fish hung and birds scattered— in the end they were able to establish merit and accomplish affairs, restoring and making whole the altars of soil and grain— can one say only Heaven aided? It is also human planning.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient Yan, Qi, Chu, and Yue fell to ruin, yet their heirs rebuilt them— not heaven alone but human resolve.

sentences.zh: 向使懷苟存之計，納譙周之言，何邦基之能構，令名之可獲哉？

translations.literal: If formerly one had embraced a plan of barely surviving and accepted Qiao Zhou's words— how could state foundations be built, how could a fair name be obtained!
translations.idiomatic: Had Liu Shan clung only to survival and heeded Zhou, what foundation or fame could he have won?

sentences.zh: 禪既闇主，周實駑臣，方之申包、田單、范蠡、大夫種，不亦遠乎！〉

translations.literal: Shan was already a dim lord; Zhou was truly a mediocre minister— comparing them to Shen Baoxu, Tian Dan, Fan Li, or Grandee Zhong— are they not far!"
translations.idiomatic: A dull emperor and a plodding minister are poor company for the heroes who saved their states."

sentences.zh: 時晉文王為魏相國，以周有全國之功，封陽城亭侯。

translations.literal: At the time Jin king Wen was Wei state minister; because Zhou had merit of preserving the whole state, he enfeoffed him marquis of Yangcheng village.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Zhao was Wei's minister of state, he enfeoffed Zhou as marquis of Yangcheng for saving the Liu clan.

sentences.zh: 又下書辟周，周發至漢中，困疾不進。

translations.literal: Again he issued a summons to Zhou; Zhou set out, reached Hanzhong, was blocked by illness and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao summoned him again; Zhou reached Hanzhong but illness halted him.

sentences.zh: 咸熙二年夏，巴郡文立從洛陽還蜀，過見周。

translations.literal: In summer of the second year of Xianxi, Wen Li of Ba commandery returned from Luoyang to Shu and passed to visit Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Xianxi 2, Wen Li of Ba returned from Luoyang and called on Zhou.

sentences.zh: 周語次，因書版示立曰：「典午忽兮，月酉沒兮。

translations.literal: In the course of conversation Zhou therefore wrote on a board to show Li saying, "The steward of noon wanes; the moon in you sets."
translations.idiomatic: During their talk Zhou scribbled a riddle: "The steward of noon wanes" punned on the house of Sima; "the moon in you sets" pointed to the eighth month of the calendar.

sentences.zh: 」典午者謂司馬也，月酉者謂八月也，至八月而文王果崩。

translations.literal: Dianwu means the Sima; moon you means the eighth month; by the eighth month king Wen indeed collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: "Dianwu" punned on the house of Sima; "moon you" pointed to the eighth month— and Sima Zhao died that August.

sentences.zh: 〈《華陽國志》曰：文立字廣休，少治毛詩、三禮，兼通羣書。

translations.literal: The Huayang Guo zhi states: Li's courtesy name was Guangxiu; in youth he studied Mao Poetry and the three ritual classics and also penetrated many books.
translations.idiomatic: The Huayang Guo zhi names Wen Li as Guangxiu, trained in the Mao Odes, the three rituals, and general literature.

sentences.zh: 刺史費禕命為從事，入為尚書郎，復辟禕大將軍東曹掾，稍遷尚書。

translations.literal: Inspector Fei Yi ordered him as adjutant; he entered as gentleman of the Masters of Writing; again was summoned as eastern bureau clerk to grand general Yi; gradually transferred to director.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yi made him adjutant, then a court secretary, then a staff officer under the grand general, and finally a director.

sentences.zh: 蜀並於魏，梁州建，首為別駕從事，舉秀才。

translations.literal: When Shu was annexed by Wei, Liangzhou was established; he first became chief clerk on tour, was raised flourishing talent.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu fell he became chief clerk when Liangzhou was organized and was recommended as flourishing talent.

sentences.zh: 晉泰始二年，拜濟陰太守，遷太子中庶子。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jin Taishi he was appointed administrator of Jiyin, transferred to junior tutor to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi 2 of the Jin he became prefect of Jiyin, then junior tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 立上言：「故蜀大官及盡忠死事者子孫，雖仕郡國，或有不才，同之齊民為劇；

translations.literal: Li submitted saying, "Former Shu high officials and descendants of those who died loyally for affairs— although they serve commanderies and states, some lack talent; treating them the same as common folk is harsh;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that sons of Shu officials who had died for the state should not be lumped with commoners if untalented;

sentences.zh: 又諸葛亮、蔣琬、費禕等子孫流徙中畿，各宜量才敘用，以慰巴、蜀之心，傾吳人之望。

translations.literal: moreover Zhuge Liang, Jiang Wan, Fei Yi, and others' descendants drift in the central domain— each ought to be employed according to ability, to comfort Ba and Shu hearts and tilt Wu people's expectation."
translations.idiomatic: and that the stranded heirs of Liang, Wan, and Yi deserved measured appointments to reassure Ba-Shu and impress Wu."

sentences.zh: 」事皆施行。

translations.literal: The matters were all carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted his proposals.

sentences.zh: 轉散騎常侍，獻可替否，多所補納。

translations.literal: He was transferred to supernumerary palace attendant, offering what was fit and replacing what was not— much was remedied and taken in.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to supernumerary palace attendant and remonstrated effectively on policy.

sentences.zh: 稍遷衛尉，中朝服其賢雅，為時名卿。

translations.literal: Gradually transferred to commandant of the guards; the central court admired his worthy refinement and he became a famed minister of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as commandant of the guards, esteemed at court as a model minister.

sentences.zh: 咸寧末卒。

translations.literal: He died at the end of Xianning.
translations.idiomatic: He died near the end of the Xianning era.

sentences.zh: 立章奏詩詩賦論頌凡數十篇。〉

translations.literal: Li's memorials, poems, rhapsodies, and disquisitions in all several tens of pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He left several dozen memorials, poems, and essays.

sentences.zh: 晉室踐阼，累下詔所在發遣周。

translations.literal: When the Jin house ascended the throne, repeatedly issued edicts to the places to dispatch Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin accession, repeated edicts ordered Zhou to the capital.

sentences.zh: 周遂輿疾詣洛，泰始三年至。

translations.literal: Zhou thereupon in a litter with illness went to Luo; in the third year of Taishi he arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou was carried to Luoyang ill and arrived in Taishi 3.

sentences.zh: 以疾不起，就拜騎都尉，周乃自陳無功而封，求還爵土，皆不聽許。

translations.literal: Because of illness he did not rise; on the spot he was appointed chief commandant of cavalry; Zhou then himself stated he had no merit yet was enfeoffed, begged to return noble rank and soil— all were not listened to or permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Too ill to bow, he was named chief commandant of cavalry; he protested that he deserved no fief, but the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 五年，予常為本郡中正，清定事訖，求休還家，往與周別。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, your servant Songzhi served as impartial judge of my commandery; when clearing affairs was finished, I sought rest and return home, went to bid Zhou farewell.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Pei Songzhi served as local impartial judge for his home commandery; when the roster work ended he visited Zhou to say goodbye.

sentences.zh: 周語予曰：「昔孔子七十二、劉向、楊雄七十一而沒，今吾年過七十，庶慕孔子遺風，可與劉、楊同軌，恐不出後歲，必便長逝，不復相見矣。

translations.literal: Zhou spoke to me saying, "In old days Confucius at seventy-two, Liu Xiang and Yang Xiong at seventy-one then died; now my years pass seventy; I hope to emulate Confucius' bequeathed air— may share the track with Liu and Yang; I fear before the next year I will certainly pass away long, and we will not again meet."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou told him, "Confucius died at seventy-two, Liu Xiang and Yang Xiong at seventy-one. I am past seventy and hope to match their span— I doubt we shall meet again after next year."

sentences.zh: 」疑周以術知之，假而此言也。

translations.literal: Your servant suspected Zhou by arts knew it, borrowing this to say it.
translations.idiomatic: Songzhi suspected Zhou divined his end and spoke in riddles.

sentences.zh: 六年秋，為散騎常侍，疾篤不拜，至冬卒。

translations.literal: In autumn of the sixth year he was made supernumerary palace attendant; gravely ill he did not accept the appointment; by winter he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year's autumn he was named supernumerary palace attendant but was too ill to serve; he died that winter.

sentences.zh: 〈《晉陽秋》載詔曰：「朕甚悼之，賜朝服一具，衣一襲，錢十五萬。

translations.literal: The Jin Yang Autumn records an edict saying, "We deeply mourn him, grant one set of court robes, one suit of clothes, one hundred fifty thousand cash."
translations.idiomatic: The Jin Yang Autumn preserves an edict mourning him with robes and cash.

sentences.zh: 」周息熙上言，周臨終屬熙曰：「久抱疾，未曾朝見，若國恩賜朝服衣物者，勿以加身。

translations.literal: Zhou's son Xi submitted saying: Zhou on the verge of death instructed Xi saying, "Long I have embraced illness, never having audience at court; if the state grace grants court robes and clothing, do not let them be put on the body.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xi reported Zhou's deathbed wish that imperial gifts of dress not be placed on his corpse.

sentences.zh: 當還舊墓，道險行難，豫作輕棺。

translations.literal: We ought to return to the old tomb; the road is perilous and travel hard— beforehand make a light coffin.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for a light coffin for the hard road home to his old grave.

sentences.zh: 殯斂已畢，上還所賜。

translations.literal: When laying out and encoffining was finished, upward return what was granted.
translations.idiomatic: After the rites, return the gifts to the throne.

sentences.zh: 」詔還衣服，給棺直。〉

translations.literal: The edict returned the clothes and supplied coffin expense."
translations.idiomatic: The court returned the robes and paid for the coffin instead."

sentences.zh: 凡所著述，擇定《法訓》、《五經論》、《古史考》書之屬百餘篇。

translations.literal: In all that he authored and set in order— the Norms of Law, Disquisitions on the Five Classics, Investigations of Ancient History, and writings of that class— more than a hundred pieces.
translations.idiomatic: His corpus includes over a hundred titles such as the Norms of Law, the Five Classics treatises, and the Investigations of Ancient History.

sentences.zh: 〈益部耆舊傳曰：益州刺史董榮圖畫周像於州學，命從事李通頌之曰：「抑抑譙侯，好古述儒，寶道懷真，鑑世盈虛，雅名美跡，終始是書。

translations.literal: The elders' tradition of Yi states: Yi Province inspector Dong Rong painted Zhou's likeness at the provincial school and ordered adjutant Li Tong to hymn him saying, "Stately, stately Lord Qiao, loving antiquity and transmitting Confucians, treasuring the way and cherishing truth, mirroring the world's fullness and void, fair name and fine traces— from first to last are written in books.
translations.idiomatic: The Yi elders' record tells how Inspector Dong Rong hung Zhou's portrait in the school and had Li Tong compose a hymn praising his scholarship and judgment.

sentences.zh: 我後欽賢，無言不譽，攀諸前哲，丹青是圖。

translations.literal: Our later ruler esteems worthies— no word not praised; climbing the former sages, cinnabar and green are the picture.
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign honors the worthy and sets their image in paint for posterity.

sentences.zh: 嗟爾來葉，鑑茲顯模。」〉

translations.literal: Alas you later leaves, mirror this shining model."
translations.idiomatic: O later generations, take this portrait as your mirror."

sentences.zh: 孫 譙秀

translations.literal: Grandson: Qiao Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson: Qiao Xiu.

sentences.zh: 周三子，熙、賢、同，少子同頗好周業，亦以忠篤質素為行，舉孝廉，除錫令、東宮洗馬，召不就。

translations.literal: Zhou had three sons, Xi, Xian, and Tong; the youngest son Tong quite loved Zhou's profession; also by loyalty, solidity, plainness as conduct, was recommended filial and incorrupt, appointed magistrate of Xi, washed horse of the eastern palace— summoned, did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's three sons were Xi, Xian, and Tong. Tong followed his father's studies, earned recommendation as filial and incorrupt, was named magistrate of Xi and tutor to the heir, but refused the summons.

sentences.zh: 〈周長子熙。

translations.literal: Zhou's eldest son was Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's eldest son was Xi.

sentences.zh: 熙子秀，字元彥。

translations.literal: Xi's son Xiu, courtesy name Yuanyan.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's son Qiao Xiu bore the courtesy name Yuanyan.

sentences.zh: 《晉陽秋》曰：秀性清靜，不交於世，知將大亂，豫絕人事，從兄弟及諸親裡不與相見。

translations.literal: The Jin Yang Autumn states: Xiu's nature was quiet and still, did not mingle with the world; knowing great chaos would come, beforehand cut off human affairs; with cousins and various kin in the village he did not meet.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin Yang Autumn says Qiao Xiu was reclusive, foresaw chaos, broke off social ties, and would not even see kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 州郡辟命，及李雄盜蜀，安車徵秀，又雄叔父驤、驤子壽辟命，皆不應。

translations.literal: Province and commandery summoned with mandate, and when Li Xiong robbed Shu, summoned Xiu with comfortable carriage; again Xiong's uncle Fu and Fu's son Shou summoned with mandate— all he did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: He ignored every summons, including Li Xiong's carriage call and offers from Li Xiong's kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 常冠鹿皮，躬耕山藪。

translations.literal: He constantly capped deer skin and personally plowed mountain marsh.
translations.idiomatic: He wore a deerskin cap and farmed the hills in seclusion.

sentences.zh: 永和三年，安西將軍桓溫平蜀，表薦秀曰：「臣聞大樸既虧，則高尚之標顯；

translations.literal: In the third year of Yonghe, General Who Pacifies the West Huan Wen pacified Shu; in a memorial recommending Xiu he said, "Your servant has heard that when great simplicity is already deficient, then the mark of the lofty is displayed;
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghe 3, Huan Wen conquered Shu and recommended Xiu: "When simplicity is lost, recluses shine forth;

sentences.zh: 道喪時昏，則忠貞之義彰。

translations.literal: when the way is lost and the age dark, then the meaning of loyalty and steadfastness is manifest."
translations.idiomatic: when the age grows dark, steadfast loyalty stands out."

sentences.zh: 故有洗耳投淵以振玄邈之風，亦有秉心矯跡以惇在三之節。

translations.literal: Therefore some washed ears and cast into abyss to shake the wind of dark remoteness; some also grasped mind and straightened tracks to thicken the integrity of the three bonds."
translations.idiomatic: Some fled the world to cleanse their ears; others held fast to duty to honor the three bonds."

sentences.zh: 是以上代之君，莫不崇重斯軌，所以篤俗訓民，靜一流競。

translations.literal: Therefore rulers of high antiquity, none did not honor and weight this track— by it to thicken custom and instruct the people, quieting the one flow of contention.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient kings always honored such men to steady the people and quell strife.

sentences.zh: 伏惟大晉應符禦世，運無常通，時有屯蹇，神州丘墟，三方圮裂，兔罝絕響於中林，白駒無聞於空谷，斯有識之所悼心，大雅之所嘆息者也。

translations.literal: We humbly think great Jin received the talisman and governs the age; fortune has no constant passage; times have obstruction and hardship; the divine region is mound and ruin; three sides are broken and split; the rabbit snare has cut off sound in the central forest; the white colt has no hearing in empty valleys— this is what the knowing mourn in heart and what the great ya sighs over."
translations.idiomatic: Great Jin rules a broken age: the heartland lies waste, the realm is split, worthies hide like the Book of Songs' lost hunters and white colts— a grief to every thoughtful man."

sentences.zh: 陛下聖德嗣興，方恢天緒。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's sagely virtue succeeds and rises; you are just restoring Heaven's thread.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty renews the mandate of heaven.

sentences.zh: 臣昔奉役，有事西土，鯨鯢既縣，思宣大化；

translations.literal: Your servant formerly served on campaign, having business in the western land; now that the great fish are hung, I think to spread great transformation;
translations.idiomatic: I once campaigned in the west; now that the rebels are cut down, I would extend your transforming influence;

sentences.zh: 訪諸故老，搜楊潛逸，庶武羅於羿、浞之墟，想王蠋於亡齊之境。

translations.literal: I visited various old elders, searched and raised the hidden and reclusive, hoping in the ruins of Yi and Zhuo to spread Wu's net, thinking of Wang Zhu in the border of lost Qi."
translations.idiomatic: I sought old men and hidden talent as archers once hunted Yi and Zhuo, hoping to find another Wang Zhu among the lost."

sentences.zh: 竊聞巴西譙秀，植操貞固，抱德肥遁，揚清渭波。

translations.literal: Privately I have heard that Qiao Xiu of Ba commandery, plants conduct chaste and firm, embraces virtue and fatly hides, raising purity on the Wei waves."
translations.idiomatic: I hear that Qiao Xiu of Ba is incorruptible, virtuous, and reclusive as a clear stream.

sentences.zh: 於時皇極遘道消之會，羣黎蹈顛沛之艱，中華有顧瞻之哀，幽谷無遷喬之望；

translations.literal: At this time the royal apex meets the meeting of the way's waning; the host of black-haired tread the hardship of overturning and ruin; central Hua has the grief of looking back; deep valleys have no hope of moving to tall trees;
translations.idiomatic: The throne totters, the people suffer, the heartland mourns, and no phoenix rises from the wilds;

sentences.zh: 凶命屢招，姦威仍偪，身寄虎吻，危同朝露，而能抗節玉立，誓不降辱，杜門絕跡，不面偽庭，進免龔勝亡身之禍，退無薛方詭之譏；

translations.literal: fierce mandates repeatedly summon; treacherous might still presses; body lodged in tiger muzzle, peril same as morning dew— yet able to resist integrity and stand like jade, swearing not to descend to insult, blocking gate and cutting off tracks, not facing the false court; advancing avoids Gong Sheng's calamity of destroying body, retreating lacks Xue Fang's ridicule of guile;
translations.idiomatic: yet Xiu defies threats, shuts his gate, will not bow to usurpers, avoids Gong Sheng's suicide and Xue Fang's hypocrisy;

sentences.zh: 雖園、綺之棲商、洛，管寧之默遼海，方之於秀，殆無以過。

translations.literal: although Yuan and Qi's dwelling at Shang and Luo, Guanning's silence by the Liao sea— compared to Xiu, probably nothing surpasses."
translations.idiomatic: he matches the recluses of Shang-Luo and Guan Ning at Liaodong— perhaps none surpass him."

sentences.zh: 於今西土，以為美談。

translations.literal: In the present western land, people take it as fine talk.
translations.idiomatic: The west still tells his story with admiration.

sentences.zh: 夫旌德禮賢，化道之所先，崇表殊節，聖哲之上務。

translations.literal: For displaying virtue and ritually treating worthies is what transforming the way puts first; exalting the mark of extraordinary integrity is the sage's upper task.
translations.idiomatic: Honoring recluses is the first duty of moral government.

sentences.zh: 方今六合未康，豺狼當路，遺黎偷薄，義聲弗聞，益宜振起道義之徒，以敦流遁之弊。

translations.literal: Just now the six directions are not yet tranquil; jackals and wolves block the road; surviving people are mean and thin; righteous sound is not heard— all the more ought one to rouse those who uphold the way, to thicken the evil of drifting and fleeing."
translations.idiomatic: With the realm still torn by wolves and the people cynical, you should lift up men of principle to cure flight from duty.

sentences.zh: 若秀蒙薄帛之徵，足以鎮靜頹風，軌訓囂俗；

translations.literal: If Xiu received the summons of thin silks, it would be enough to quiet the collapsing wind, to track and instruct the noisy vulgar;
translations.idiomatic: A modest summons to Xiu would steady custom and shame the vulgar;

sentences.zh: 幽遐仰流，九服知化矣。

translations.literal: the hidden and far will look up to the flowing transformation; the nine garments will know transformation."
translations.idiomatic: the distant would look to your virtue and the nine provinces would feel your sway."

sentences.zh: 」及蕭敬叛亂，避難宕渠川中，鄉人宗族馮依者以百數。

translations.literal: When Xiao Jing rebelled in disorder, he avoided calamity in the Dangqu rivers; fellow villagers and clan kin who depended on him numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Jing rose in revolt, Xiu fled into the Dangqu valleys with hundreds of kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 秀年八十，眾人以其薦老，欲代之負擔，秀拒曰：「各有老弱，當先營救。

translations.literal: Xiu was eighty; the crowd because he was aged wished to carry his load for him; Xiu refused saying, "Each has old and weak— you ought first to plan rescue.
translations.idiomatic: At eighty the refugees offered to carry his pack; he refused: "Everyone has elders to save first.

sentences.zh: 吾氣力自足堪此，不以垂朽之年累諸君也。

translations.literal: My breath and strength are enough to bear this; I will not with nearly rotten years burden you gentlemen."
translations.idiomatic: I still have strength enough— do not waste it on an old man."

sentences.zh: 」後十餘年，卒於家。〉

translations.literal: After more than ten years he died at home."
translations.idiomatic: He died at home more than a decade later."

sentences.zh: 郤正字令先，河南偃師人也。

translations.literal: Xi Zheng, courtesy name Lingxian, was a man of Yanshi in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zheng, courtesy name Lingxian, came from Yanshi in Henan.

sentences.zh: 祖父儉，靈帝末為益州刺史，為盜賊所殺。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jian, at the end of Lingdi was inspector of Yi Province, was killed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xi Jian was inspector of Yi Province under Emperor Ling and was killed by bandits.

sentences.zh: 會天下大亂，故正父揖因留蜀。

translations.literal: It happened the realm was in great chaos; therefore Zheng's father Yi because of it remained in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When the empire collapsed, his father Xi Yi stayed behind in Shu.

sentences.zh: 揖為將軍孟達都督，隨達降魏，為中書令史。

translations.literal: Yi was chief of staff to general Meng Da; following Da he surrendered to Wei and became clerk of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Yi served as Meng Da's chief of staff, followed him to Wei, and became a secretariat clerk.

sentences.zh: 正本名纂。

translations.literal: Zheng's original name was Zuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng had first been named Zuan.

sentences.zh: 少以父死母嫁，單煢雙立，而安貧好學，博覽墳籍。

translations.literal: In youth because father died and mother remarried, alone and solitary he stood, yet was content with poverty and fond of learning, broadly viewing the tomb classics.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned when his father died and his mother remarried, he lived alone in poverty but read every classic he could find.

sentences.zh: 弱冠能屬文，入為秘書吏，轉為令史，遷郎，至令。

translations.literal: At the capping twenty he could compose texts; he entered as clerk of the secretariat, transferred to clerk, promoted to gentleman, reaching director.
translations.idiomatic: He could write at twenty, joined the palace secretariat as a clerk, rose to secretary, then gentleman, and finally director.

sentences.zh: 性淡於榮利，而尤耽意文章，自司馬、王、揚、班、傅、張、蔡之儔遺文篇賦，及當世美書善論，益部有者，則鑽鑿推求，略皆寓目。

translations.literal: His nature was bland toward glory and profit, yet especially he addicted his mind to letters; from Sima, Wang, Yang, Ban, Fu, Zhang, Cai and their class left writings, rhapsodies, and present age fine books and good disquisitions— whatever Yi had in surplus, then he bored and chiseled and pushed seeking, in outline all lodged in the eye.
translations.idiomatic: He cared little for rank but devoured literature, hunting down every essay by Sima Qian, Wang Chong, Yang Xiong, Ban Gu, Fu, Zhang, Cai Yong, and the best writers of his own day that could be found in Shu.

sentences.zh: 自在內職，與宦人黃皓比屋周旋，經三十年。

translations.literal: From the time he was in inner office, with eunuch Huang Hao he turned in circles in neighboring houses— through thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: For thirty years he worked next door to the eunuch Huang Hao.

sentences.zh: 皓從微至貴，操弄威權，正既不為皓所愛，亦不為皓所憎，是以宮不過六百石，而免於憂患。

translations.literal: Hao from low rose to noble, wielding and toying with awesome power; Zheng was neither loved by Hao nor hated by Hao— therefore although office did not pass six hundred piculs, he escaped worry and calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Hao rose from nothing to dominate the court; Zheng stayed beneath his notice and never rose above six hundred piculs yet avoided disaster.

sentences.zh: 依則先儒，假文見意，號曰：《釋譏》，其文繼於崔駰《達旨》。

translations.literal: Relying on precedent of former Confucians, borrowing letters to show intent, he styled it Explaining Ridicule; its text continues from Cui Yin's Expressing the Aim.
translations.idiomatic: He modeled his work on the Confucian masters and titled it Explaining Ridicule, in the tradition of Cui Yin's Expressing the Aim.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：

translations.literal: Its words say,
translations.idiomatic: It begins:

sentences.zh: 或有譏余者曰：『聞之前記，夫事與時並，名與功偕，然則名之與事，前哲之急務也。

translations.literal: Someone who ridiculed me said, "I have heard in former records that affairs march with the times and names join with merit; then names and affairs are the urgent task of former sages."
translations.idiomatic: A critic tells me: "The wise say fame must match deeds and the times—"

sentences.zh: 是故創製作範，匪時不立，流稱垂名，匪功不記，名必須功而乃顯，事亦俟時以行止，身沒名滅，君子所恥。

translations.literal: Therefore establishing models and making norms— if the time is not right they are not set; spreading fame and handing down name— if merit is not there it is not recorded; name must wait for merit then is manifest, affairs also await the time to move or stop; when the body perishes and the name is extinguished, the gentleman is ashamed."
translations.idiomatic: so models fit the age and names follow achievement; to die forgotten shames a gentleman."

sentences.zh: 是以達人研道，探頤索微，觀天運之符表，考人事之盛衰，辯者馳說，智者應機，謀夫演略，武士奮威，雲合霧集，風激電飛，量時揆宜，用取世資，小屈大申，存公忽私，雖尺枉而尋直，終揚光以發輝也。

translations.literal: Therefore the man who penetrates studies the way, probes the jaw and seeks the subtle, observes Heaven's movement's tally and sign, examines human affairs' flourishing and decline; debaters gallop persuasions, wise men meet the moment, strategists unfold plans, martial knights rouse awe; clouds join and fog gathers, wind spurs and lightning flies; measuring the time and sizing what is fit, using it to take worldly resources, small bend and great stretch, preserving the public and slighting the self— although a foot bends yet a span is straight, in the end he raises radiance to send forth brilliance."
translations.idiomatic: The adept reads heaven and man, seizes the moment, bends when he must and straightens when he can, and ends in glory."

sentences.zh: 今三方鼎跱，九有未乂，悠悠四海，嬰丁禍敗，嗟道義之沉塞，愍生民之顛沛，此誠聖賢拯救之秋，烈士樹功之會也。

translations.literal: Now the three sides stand like tripod legs; the nine domains are not yet ordered; long, long the four seas, infants and adults meet calamity and defeat— alas that the way and righteousness are choked and blocked, pity that the living people are overturned and adrift— this is truly the autumn when sages and worthies rescue and the meeting when stalwarts plant merit."
translations.idiomatic: Today the realm is a tripod of rivals, the people suffer— this is the hour for heroes to save the age."

sentences.zh: 吾子以高朗之才，珪璋之質，兼覽博窺，留心道術，無遠不致，無幽不悉；

translations.literal: You, sir, with high and bright talent, jade tablet and jade scepter substance, together viewing and broadly peering, fixing mind on the way and arts— nothing far you do not reach, nothing hidden you do not exhaust;
translations.idiomatic: You have talent and character, study far and wide,

sentences.zh: 挺身取命，幹茲奧秘，躊躇紫闥，喉舌是執，九考不移，有入無出，

translations.literal: straightening body to take mandate, managing this profound secret, hesitating at the purple gate, holding the throat and tongue— nine examinations without shifting, having entry without exit,
translations.idiomatic: bear office at court as spokesman, pass nine reviews without demotion,

sentences.zh: 〈《尚書》曰：三載考績，三考黜陟幽明。

translations.literal: The Documents says: Every three years examine merit; after three examinations demote the dim and promote the bright."
translations.idiomatic: as the Documents says: three reviews in nine years set rank."

sentences.zh: 九考則二十七年。〉

translations.literal: Nine examinations then is twenty-seven years."
translations.idiomatic: Nine reviews mean twenty-seven years in office.

sentences.zh: 究古今之真偽，計時務得失。

translations.literal: Investigate antiquity and modernity's true and false, calculate the gains and losses of timely affairs.
translations.idiomatic: You weigh past and present and judge policy.

sentences.zh: 雖時獻一策，偶進一言，釋彼官責，慰此素餐，固未能輸竭忠款，盡瀝胸肝，排方入直，惠彼黎元，俾吾徒草鄙並有聞焉也。

translations.literal: Although sometimes you present one stratagem, occasionally advance one word, releasing that official responsibility, comforting this plain eating— solidly you cannot exhaustively pour out loyal sincerity, fully drip liver and lungs, push aside the square and enter the straight, show favor to those black-haired, cause our class of grass and mean together to have hearing."
translations.idiomatic: Yet an occasional memo hardly discharges your duty to the people or redeems a salary eaten in vain.

sentences.zh: 盍亦綏衡綏轡，回軌易塗，輿安駕肆，思馬斯徂，審歷揭以投濟，要夷庚之赫憮，播秋蘭以芳世，副吾徒之彼圖，不亦盛與！

translations.literal: Why not also ease the yoke and slack the reins, turn the track and change the road, ride in peace and drive at leisure, think the horses there go; examine wading deep and shallow to cast for the ford, seek the bright anxiety of the smooth road; sow autumn orchid to fragrance the age, answer our class's other plan— is it not also grand!"
translations.idiomatic: Why not change course, ease your pace, choose a safer ford, plant virtue for the age, and meet the world's hopes?"

sentences.zh: 』余聞而歎曰：『嗚呼，有若雲乎邪！

translations.literal: I heard and sighed saying, "Alas— can there really be such talk!"
translations.idiomatic: I sighed, "What empty talk is this?"

sentences.zh: 夫人心不同，實若其面，子雖光麗，既美且艷，管窺筐舉，守厥所見，未可以言八紘之形埒，信萬事之精練也。

translations.literal: Men's hearts are not the same— truly like their faces; although you, sir, are bright and beautiful, both fine and lovely, looking through a tube and lifting a basket, guarding what you have seen, you cannot yet speak of the form and boundary of the eight cords, trust in the refined mastery of the myriad affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Hearts differ like faces; your pretty speech and narrow view cannot map the whole world."

sentences.zh: 』或人率爾，仰而揚衡曰：『是何言與！

translations.literal: The someone rashly, lifting head and raising the crossbar, said, "What words are these!"
translations.idiomatic: The man cried, "What words are these!"

sentences.zh: 是何言與！』」

translations.literal: What words are these!"
translations.idiomatic: How can you say such a thing!"

sentences.zh: 余應之曰：「虞帝以面從為戒，孔聖以悅己為尤。

translations.literal: I answered saying, "Shun the emperor took face-following as warning; Kong the sage took pleasing oneself as fault.
translations.idiomatic: I replied, "Shun warned against flattery; Confucius condemned self-satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 若子之言，良我所思，將為吾子論而釋之。

translations.literal: If it is as you, sir, say— truly what I ponder— I will for you, sir, discuss and explain it."
translations.idiomatic: If that is your point, it is worth answering— hear me out."

sentences.zh: 昔在鴻荒，朦昧肇初，三皇應菉，五帝承符，爰暨夏、商，前典攸書。

translations.literal: In old days in vast chaos, dim and dark at the first beginning, the three August Ones responded to the reed chart, the five Di received the talisman; down to Xia and Shang, former canons thereupon were written.
translations.idiomatic: In primordial chaos the sage-kings answered heaven's signs; by Xia and Shang the pattern was already written in the classics.

sentences.zh: 姬衰道缺，霸者冀扶，嬴氏慘虐，吞嚼八區，於是從橫雲起，狙詐如星，奇衺蠭動，智故萌生；

translations.literal: When Ji declined, the way lacked; hegemons hoped to prop; the Ying clan cruelly tyrannized, chewing and swallowing the eight regions; then vertical and horizontal like clouds arose, snare and deceit like stars, strange perversity swarmed like bees, clever tricks sprouted;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou decayed, the way broke; hegemons vied to shore it up; Qin devoured the realm; strategists and frauds swarmed like stars.

sentences.zh: 或飾真以仇偽，或挾邪以干榮，或詭道以要上，或鬻技以自矜；

translations.literal: some adorned truth to hate the false, some clasped perversity to strike at glory, some used crooked paths to importune superiors, some hawked skills to boast themselves;
translations.idiomatic: Some masked greed as principle, some sold vice as virtue, some schemed for favor, some peddled cleverness;

sentences.zh: 背正崇邪，棄直就佞，忠無定分，義無常經。

translations.literal: they turned their backs on straightness and honored crookedness, abandoned the upright and approached flattery— loyalty had no fixed allotment, righteousness no constant warp.
translations.idiomatic: straight loyalty was abandoned for whatever won office.

sentences.zh: 故鞅法窮而慝作，斯義敗而姦成，呂門大而宗滅，韓辯立而身刑。

translations.literal: Therefore Shang Yang's laws ended and wickedness arose; Li Si's righteousness failed and treachery succeeded; the Lü gate grew great and the clan was extinguished; Han Fei's disputation stood and his person suffered punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Shang Yang's rigor bred cruelty, Li Si's "justice" bred treason, Lü Buwei's power destroyed his house, Han Fei's logic cost his life.

sentences.zh: 夫何故哉？

translations.literal: What was the reason?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 利回其心，寵耀其目，赫赫龍章，鑠鑠車服。

translations.literal: Profit turned their hearts; favor dazzled their eyes; blazing dragon insignia, flashing chariot and robes.
translations.idiomatic: Profit blinded them, rank dazzled them— dragon badges, gleaming carriages.

sentences.zh: 偷幸苟得，如反如仄，淫邪荒迷，恣睢自極，和鸞未調而身在轅側，庭寧未踐而櫟折榱覆。

translations.literal: Stealing luck and grasping gain, like overturning like tilting, wanton and perverse, wasteland and lost, wantonly cruel to the utmost; harmony bells not yet tuned yet the body was at the axle-side; courtyard calm not yet trodden yet rafter broke and ridgepole overturned.
translations.idiomatic: They snatched fortune like tipping a cart, raced into debauchery, and crashed before the bells of good rule ever rang.

sentences.zh: 天收其精，地縮其澤，人吊其躬，鬼芟其額。

translations.literal: Heaven gathered in their essence, earth shrank their moisture, men mourned their persons, ghosts mowed their foreheads.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth withdrew favor; men and spirits marked them for ruin.

sentences.zh: 初升高岡，終隕幽壑，朝含榮潤，夕為枯魄。

translations.literal: At first they climbed high hills; in the end they fell into deep ravines; at dawn they held glory's moisture; by evening they were withered souls.
translations.idiomatic: They rose at dawn in splendor and by dusk were dry bones in the pit.

sentences.zh: 是以賢人君子，深圖遠慮，畏彼咎戾，超然高舉，寧曳屬於塗中，穢濁世之休譽。

translations.literal: Therefore worthy men and gentlemen deeply planned and thought far, feared that guilt and fault, transcendentally rose high— rather trail hem in mud, foul the age's fine praise.
translations.idiomatic: So the wise feared disgrace, chose reclusion in the mire, and scorned hollow fame.

sentences.zh: 彼豈輕主慢民，而忽於時務哉？

translations.literal: Did they lightly despise lord and slow the people, and neglect timely affairs?
translations.idiomatic: They did not scorn ruler or people— they feared the times.

sentences.zh: 蓋《易》著行止之戒，《詩》有靖恭之歎，乃神之聽之而道使之然也。

translations.literal: It is because the Changes sets forth warnings on moving and stopping, the Odes has sighs over quiet reverence— then the spirits listen to it and the way makes it so."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes warns when to act or halt; the Odes praises quiet reverence— heaven hears such choices."

sentences.zh: 自我大漢，應天順民，政治之隆，皓若陽春，俯憲坤典，仰式乾文。

translations.literal: From our great Han, answering Heaven and following the people, the height of governance was bright as high spring; bowing we model the earth's canon, looking up we take pattern from Heaven's patterns.
translations.idiomatic: Our Han answered heaven and the people; its golden age shone like spring; we took law from earth and pattern from sky.

sentences.zh: 播皇澤以熙世，揚茂化之酢醇，君臣覆度，各守厥真，上垂詢納之弘，下有匡救之責，士無虛華之寵，民有一行之跡，粲乎亹亹，尚此忠益。

translations.literal: It spread imperial grace to brighten the age, raised luxuriant transformation's rich brew; ruler and minister doubled the measure, each guarding his truth; above hung the vastness of inquiry and acceptance, below lay the duty of rescue and correction; knights had no empty-glory favor, the people had traces of one good deed— splendid, diligent, they honored this loyal benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Ruler and minister shared one measure; the throne sought counsel, officials owed remonstrance; merit replaced puffery, and the realm thrived on plain duty.

sentences.zh: 然而道有隆窳，物有興廢，有聲有寂，有光有翳。

translations.literal: Yet the way has heights and hollows; things have rise and fall; there is sound and there is silence, there is light and there is shade.
translations.idiomatic: Yet every way waxes and wanes; every age knows light and shadow.

sentences.zh: 朱陽否於素秋，玄陰抑於孟春，羲和逝而望舒系，運氣匿而耀靈陳。

translations.literal: Vermilion sun was blocked in white autumn; black yin was pressed in first spring; Xi He departed and Wang Shu was tied; moving breath hid and the dazzling spirit was displayed.
translations.idiomatic: The bright sun can fail in autumn frost; the dark moon can rule an early spring— cosmic breath shifts and the shining spirit shows or hides.

sentences.zh: 沖、質不永，桓、靈墜敗，英雄雲布，豪傑蓋世，家挾殊議，人懷異計。

translations.literal: Chong and Zhi did not last long; Huan and Ling fell in ruin; heroes spread like clouds, hegemons covered the age; each household clasped a different opinion, each man cherished a different plan.
translations.idiomatic: Young emperors died young; Huan and Ling brought ruin; heroes clouded the land, each house nursing its own plot.

sentences.zh: 故從橫者欻披其胸。

translations.literal: Therefore the vertical-and-horizontal men suddenly split their breasts open.
translations.idiomatic: The strategists tore their hearts open in debate.

sentences.zh: 狙詐者暫吐其舌也。

translations.literal: The snare-and-deceit men briefly stuck out their tongues.
translations.idiomatic: The sophists shot off clever talk.

sentences.zh: 今天綱已綴，德樹西鄰，丕顯祖之宏規，縻好爵於士人，興五教以訓俗，豐九德濟民，肅明祀以礿祭，幾皇道以輔真。

translations.literal: Now the celestial net is already strung; virtue is planted in the western neighbor; displaying the grand norm of the founding ancestor, tying fine noble rank to scholars, raising the five teachings to instruct custom, enriching the nine virtues to aid the people, solemnly clarifying sacrifice to perform the spring offering, nearing the royal way to assist the true.
translations.idiomatic: Today Wei has refastened heaven's net, planted virtue in the west, honors its founders, ennobles scholars, teaches the five relations, cultivates the nine virtues, tends the altars, and walks the kingly way.

sentences.zh: 雖跱者未一，偽者未分，聖人垂戒，蓋均無貧；

translations.literal: Although those who stand firm are not yet one, the false are not yet divided— the sage hangs a warning— in general there is no poverty.
translations.idiomatic: Though rivals remain and fraud still lurks, the sage's mean keeps the realm from starving.

sentences.zh: 故君臣協美於朝，黎庶欣戴於野，動若重規，靜若疊矩。

translations.literal: Therefore ruler and minister join in beauty at court, black-haired people joyfully wear on the wilds; in motion like doubled compass, in stillness like stacked square.
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside move in one compass, rest in one square.

sentences.zh: 濟濟偉彥，元凱之倫也，有過必知，顏子之仁也．侃侃庶政，冉、季之治也，鷹揚鷙騰，伊、望之事也；

translations.literal: Crowding crowding great talents, of the class of the eight Yuans and eight Kais; having fault surely knowing it— Yanzi's benevolence; boldly boldly many policies— the governance of Ran and Ji; hawk-soaring and vulture-leaping— the deeds of Yi and Wang;
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers throng like the Eight Yuans and Eight Kais; they own faults like Yan Hui, govern boldly like Ran Qiu, soar to duty like Yi Yin.

sentences.zh: 總羣俊之上略，含薛氏之三計，敷張、陳之秘策，故力徵以勤世，援化英而不遑，豈暇修枯籜於榛穢哉！

translations.literal: they sum the host of heroes' upper stratagems, contain the Xue clan's three plans, spread Zhang and Chen's secret policies— therefore with strength they campaign to toil the age, grasp transforming heroes without leisure— how could they have leisure to patch dry bamboo slips in bramble muck!
translations.idiomatic: They wield the best plans of Zhang Liang and Chen Ping— busy saving the age, they cannot fuss over dead letters in the weeds.

sentences.zh: 然吾不才，在朝累紀，托身所天，心焉是恃。

translations.literal: Yet I am without talent; in court many years I have piled; I entrust body to what Heaven makes; the heart thereby relies.
translations.idiomatic: I lack their gifts yet have served many years, trusting heaven and my sovereign.

sentences.zh: 樂滄海之廣深，歎篙岳之高跱，聞仲尼之贊商，感鄉校之益己，彼平仲之和羹，亦近可而替否；

translations.literal: I rejoice in the deep vastness of the blue sea, sigh at the height of Song mountain; I have heard Zhongni's praise of Shang, felt the village school's benefit to self; that Pingzhong's harmonizing cauldron— also is near enough to replace the bad with the good;
translations.idiomatic: I love learning like the sea, revere virtue like a peak; Confucius praised Shang, the village school taught me; even Yan Ying's "harmonizing stew" can turn counsel to good.

sentences.zh: 故矇冒瞽說，時有攸獻，譬遒人之有採於市閭，遊童之吟詠乎疆畔，庶以增廣福祥，輸力規諫。

translations.literal: Therefore blindly I risk blind speech; at times there is what I present— like the wayfarer's having gathering in market lanes, wandering boys' chanting at field edges— hoping thereby to increase and broaden blessing and auspice, to contribute force in regulation and remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: So I dare speak like a street collector of songs or a field child's rhyme— hoping to add some grain of luck and honest advice.

sentences.zh: 若其合也，則以暗協明，進應靈符；

translations.literal: If it fits, then with darkness it matches brightness, advancing answers the spirit tally;
translations.idiomatic: If I am right, shadow meets light and heaven answers;

sentences.zh: 如其違也，自我常分，退守己愚。

translations.literal: if it goes against, then from myself the constant allotment, withdrawing I guard my foolishness.
translations.idiomatic: if wrong, I keep my humble place and my silence.

sentences.zh: 進退任數，不矯不誣，循性樂天，夫何恨諸？

translations.literal: Advance and retreat follow fate, neither forcing nor lying; following nature and rejoicing in Heaven— what resentment is there?
translations.idiomatic: I advance or retire with fate, force nothing, lie about nothing, follow nature— why nurse a grudge?

sentences.zh: 此其所既入不出，有而若無者也。

translations.literal: This is what they call entering and not coming out, having yet as if not having.
translations.idiomatic: That is the "office entered but never left, duty done yet unseen."

sentences.zh: 狹屈氏之常醒，濁漁父之必醉，溷柳季之卑等辱，編夷、叔之高懟。

translations.literal: Narrow Qu Yuan's constant waking, muddy the fisher's must-be drunk, mix Liu Xia's low rank insult, compile Yi and Shu's high resentment.
translations.idiomatic: I would narrow Qu Yuan's wakefulness, cloud the fisherman's drunk wisdom, rank with Liu Xia's lowliness, yet match Boyi and Shu Qi's high scorn.

sentences.zh: 合不以得，違以不失，得不克詘，失不慘悸。

translations.literal: Joining— not because of gain; parting— not because of loss; gain does not make me cringe, loss does not make me tremble.
translations.idiomatic: I do not cling to success or flee failure; neither flattens nor terrifies me.

sentences.zh: 不樂前以顧軒，不就後以慮輊，不鬻譽以乾澤，不辭愆以忌絀。

translations.literal: I do not rejoice in the front to look at the high carriage-end, do not approach the rear to fear the low carriage-end, do not sell praise to beg moisture, do not shun fault to fear removal.
translations.idiomatic: I do not truckle to the chariot ahead or dread the one behind, hawk praise for favor, or dodge blame to keep a post.

sentences.zh: 何責之釋？

translations.literal: What responsibility is released?
translations.idiomatic: What duty have I shirked?

sentences.zh: 何餐之卹？

translations.literal: What eating is pitied?
translations.idiomatic: What salary have I stolen?

sentences.zh: 何方之排？

translations.literal: What square is pushed aside?
translations.idiomatic: What upright path have I blocked?

sentences.zh: 何直之入？

translations.literal: What straight is entered?
translations.idiomatic: What crooked path have I taken?

sentences.zh: 九考不移，固其所執也。

translations.literal: Nine examinations without shifting— solidly this is what they hold.
translations.idiomatic: Nine reviews without shifting— that is my steadfast rule.

sentences.zh: 方今朝士山積，髦俊成羣，猶鱗介之潛乎巨海，毛羽之集乎鄧林，游禽逝不為之鮮，浮魴臻不為之殷。

translations.literal: Just now court gentlemen pile like mountains, fine talents form flocks— like scales and shells hidden in the great sea, feathers gathered in the Deng forest; wandering birds pass and it is not made sparse, floating bream arrive and it is not made crowded.
translations.idiomatic: The court teems with talent like fish in the sea or birds in the forest— one more voice neither crowds nor empties it.

sentences.zh: 且陽靈幽於唐葉，陰精應於商時，陽盱請而洪災息，桑林禱而甘澤滋。

translations.literal: Moreover yang essence hid in Tang's leaf, yin essence answered in Shang's time; Yang Xu prayed and great flood ceased; mulberry grove prayed and sweet rain moistened.
translations.idiomatic: Sun and moon have their eclipses; Yu prayed at Yangxu and floods ended; Tang prayed at the mulberry grove and rain returned.

sentences.zh: 〈《淮南子》曰：禹為水，以身請於陽盱之河，湯苦旱，以身禱於桑林之際，聖人之憂民，如此其明也。

translations.literal: The Huainanzi says: Yu for the waters, with his body begged at the Yangxu river; Tang suffered bitter drought, with his body prayed at the edge of the mulberry grove— the sages' care for the people was as clear as this."
translations.idiomatic: The Huainanzi tells how Yu offered himself at Yangxu to stop floods and Tang at the mulberry grove to end drought— such was sage care for the people."

sentences.zh: 《呂氏春秋》曰：昔殷湯克夏桀而天下大旱，三年不收，湯乃以身禱於桑林曰：「余一人有罪，無及萬方，萬方有罪，在余一人，無以一人之不敏，使上帝毀傷民之大命。

translations.literal: The Lüshi Chunqiu says: In old days Yin Tang overcame Xia Jie and the realm had great drought three years without harvest; Tang then with his body prayed at the mulberry grove saying, "I alone have guilt— do not reach the myriad regions; the myriad regions have guilt— it is in me alone; do not because one man is not keen let the High Lord destroy and injure the people's great mandate."
translations.idiomatic: The Lüshi Chunqiu records Tang's prayer after conquering Jie: "Blame me, not the people; if the people suffer, the fault is mine— do not let one dull ruler cost heaven its care for life."

sentences.zh: 」湯於是剪其髮，攦其爪，自以為犧牲，用祈福於上帝。

translations.literal: Tang thereupon cut his hair, broke his nails, taking himself as sacrificial victim, used it to pray blessing to the High Lord.
translations.idiomatic: He cut his hair and nails and offered himself as a victim to heaven.

sentences.zh: 民乃甚悅。

translations.literal: The people then were very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The people rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 雨乃大至。〉

translations.literal: Rain then greatly arrived.
translations.idiomatic: The rains came in torrents.

sentences.zh: 行止有道，啟塞有期。

translations.literal: Moving and stopping have a way; opening and blocking have a season.
translations.idiomatic: Action and rest follow the way; doors open and close in season.

sentences.zh: 我師遺訓，不怨不尤，委命恭己，我又何辭？

translations.literal: Our teacher's bequeathed instruction: do not resent, do not blame; entrust mandate, respect oneself— what more have I to say?
translations.idiomatic: Confucius taught: blame neither heaven nor man; accept fate with humility— what answer need I add?

sentences.zh: 辭窮路單，將反初節，綜墳典之流勞，尋孔氏之遺藝，綴微辭以存道，儘先軌而投制，題叔肸之優遊，美疏氏之遐逝，收止足以言歸，泛皓然以容裔，欣環堵以恬娛，免咎悔於斯世，顧茲心之未泰，懼末塗之泥滯，仍求激而增憤，肆中懷以告誓。

translations.literal: With words exhausted and the road solitary, I will return to my first integrity, ordering the flowing toil of tomb classics, seeking Confucius' bequeathed arts, linking subtle phrases to preserve the way, following former tracks and casting regulation, taking Shu Xi's ease, praising the Shu clan's far departure, gathering enough to speak of returning, drifting bright and easy in vast ease, rejoicing in the ringed wall for quiet pleasure, avoiding fault and regret in this age— yet looking at this heart's not yet peace, fearing the mud mire of the last road, still seeking sharpness to increase indignation, pouring out the mid-breast to declare oath.
translations.idiomatic: When argument fails I return to the classics, follow Confucius' path in small phrases, envy the ease of Shu Xi and the flight of the hermits, hope to live content in a humble lane and escape this age's regrets— yet my heart is still uneasy, fearing the mire ahead, and I cry out this oath from my breast.

sentences.zh: 昔九方考精於至貴，秦牙沈思於殊形；

translations.literal: In old days Jiufang examined essence in the supremely noble; Qin Ya sank thought in unusual form;
translations.idiomatic: Jiufang Gao read the spirit of horses; Qin Ya studied their bones;

sentences.zh: 〈《淮南子》曰：秦穆公謂伯樂曰：「子之年長矣，子姓有可使求馬者乎？

translations.literal: The Huainanzi says: Duke Mu of Qin said to Bole, "Your years are long; among your sons and kin is there one who can be sent to seek horses?"
translations.idiomatic: The Huainanzi: Duke Mu asked Bole for a successor to find horses.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「良馬者，可以形容筋骨相也。

translations.literal: He answered saying, "For good horses, one may by form and sinew and bone examine them.
translations.idiomatic: Bole replied, "A common good horse shows in bone and sinew.

sentences.zh: 相天下之馬者，若滅若沒，若失若亡，其一若此馬者，絕塵卻轍。

translations.literal: For examining horses under heaven, if dim if vanished, if lost if gone, one like this horse— cuts dust and spurns wheel-ruts."
translations.idiomatic: A horse of heaven seems absent yet outruns dust and ruts."

sentences.zh: 臣之子皆下才也，可告以良馬而不可告以天下之馬。

translations.literal: My sons are all lower talent; I can tell them of good horses but cannot tell them of horses under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: My sons are middling; I can teach common steeds, not heaven's steeds.

sentences.zh: 天下之馬，臣有所與共儋纏採薪九方堙，此其相馬，非臣之下也，請見之。

translations.literal: Horses under heaven— I have one who together with me carries cordwood, Jiufang Ying; this one's examining horses is not below mine; please see him."
translations.idiomatic: For heaven's horses use my cordwood-gatherer Jiufang Ying— his eye matches mine— send for him."

sentences.zh: 」穆公見之，使之求馬，三月而反，報曰：「已得馬矣，在於沙丘。

translations.literal: Duke Mu saw him, sent him to seek a horse; three months he returned, reporting saying, "I have already obtained a horse; it is at Sandy Hill."
translations.idiomatic: Mu received him and sent him out; three months later he reported a horse at Sandy Hill.

sentences.zh: 」穆公曰：「何馬也？

translations.literal: Duke Mu said, "What horse?"
translations.idiomatic: "What kind of horse?" Mu asked.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「牝而黃。

translations.literal: He answered saying, "A mare, yellow."
translations.idiomatic: "A yellow mare," he said.

sentences.zh: 」使人往取之，牡而驪。

translations.literal: They sent someone to fetch it; it was a stallion, black.
translations.idiomatic: The groom brought back a black stallion.

sentences.zh: 穆公不悅，召伯樂而問之曰：「敗矣，子之所使求馬者也！

translations.literal: Duke Mu was not pleased; he summoned Bole and asked him saying, "It is ruined— the one you sent to seek horses!
translations.idiomatic: Mu was furious: "Your man is useless!

sentences.zh: 毛物牝牡尚弗能知，又何馬之能知？

translations.literal: Hair and thing, mare and stallion, he still could not know— how much more could he know horses!"
translations.idiomatic: He could not tell sex or color— how could he judge quality!"

sentences.zh: 」伯樂喟然太息曰：「一至此乎！

translations.literal: Bole sighed a long sigh saying, "Has he really reached that point!
translations.idiomatic: Bole sighed, "Has he truly reached that level!

sentences.zh: 是乃所以千萬

translations.literal: This is why he is worth ten thousand
translations.idiomatic: That is why he is worth ten thousand

translations.literal: (leagues)
translations.idiomatic: (leagues)

sentences.zh: 臣而無數者也。

translations.literal: ministers and cannot be numbered among them."
translations.idiomatic: of ordinary judges and still stands beyond count among them."

sentences.zh: 若堙之所觀者天機也，得其精而忘其粗，在其內而忘其外，見其所見而不見其所不見，視其所視而遺其所不視，若彼之所相者，乃有貴乎馬者。

translations.literal: What Ying observes is heaven's mechanism; he obtains the essence and forgets the coarse, is inside it and forgets the outside, sees what he sees and does not see what he does not see, looks at what he looks at and loses what he does not look at— what that one examines in horses then has something more precious than horses."
translations.idiomatic: Ying sees the spirit inside the beast and forgets hide and color— that is why he names heaven's horse."

sentences.zh: 」馬至，而果天下之馬也。

translations.literal: When the horse arrived, it indeed was a horse under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When the horse came, it was indeed the finest in the realm.

sentences.zh: 淮南子又曰：伯樂、寒風、秦牙、葛青，所相各異，其知馬一也；

translations.literal: The Huainanzi again says: Bole, Hanfeng, Qin Ya, Ge Qing— each examined differently; their knowing the horse was one;
translations.idiomatic: The Huainanzi lists many judges— each used a different method yet grasped the same truth;

sentences.zh: 蓋九方觀其精，秦牙察其形。〉

translations.literal: in general Jiufang observed its essence, Qin Ya inspected its form."
translations.idiomatic: Jiufang read the spirit, Qin Ya the body."

sentences.zh: 薛燭察寶以飛譽，

translations.literal: Xue Zhu examined treasure thereby to fly reputation,
translations.idiomatic: Xue Zhu judged swords and won fame,

sentences.zh: 〈《越絕書》曰：昔越王句踐有寶劍五枚，聞於天下。

translations.literal: the Yue jue shu says: In old days King Goujian of Yue had five precious swords, heard of in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: the Yue jue shu tells how Goujian of Yue owned five famous blades.

sentences.zh: 客有能相劍者名薛燭，王召而問之：「吾有寶劍五，請以示子。

translations.literal: A guest able to examine swords was named Xue Zhu; the king summoned and asked him, "I have five precious swords; I ask to show them to you, sir."
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the connoisseur Xue Zhu to view them.

sentences.zh: 」乃取豪曹、臣闕，薛燭曰：「皆非也。

translations.literal: Then he took Haocao and Juque; Xue Zhu said, "Neither is it."
translations.idiomatic: He produced Haocao and Juque; Zhu said they were not the best.

sentences.zh: 」又取純鉤、湛盧，燭曰：「觀其劍鈔，爛爛如列宿之行，觀其光，渾渾如水之將溢於塘，觀其文，渙渙如冰將釋，此所謂純鉤邪？

translations.literal: Again he took Chunjun and Zhanlu; Zhu said, "Looking at its blade edge, blazing like a march of stars; looking at its gleam, rolling like water about to overflow the pond; looking at its pattern, flowing like ice about to melt— this is what is called Chunjun, is it not?"
translations.idiomatic: When shown Chunjun and Zhanlu he praised the starry edge, the watery gleam, the melting-ice grain— "This is Chunjun."

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「是也。

translations.literal: The king said, "It is so."
translations.idiomatic: The king agreed.

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「客有直之者，有市之鄉三，駿馬千匹，千戶之都二，可乎？

translations.literal: The king said, "If a guest has one straight to it— three market towns, a thousand swift horses, two thousand-household capitals— can it be?"
translations.idiomatic: The king offered three towns, a thousand horses, and two capitals of a thousand households for the sword.

sentences.zh: 」薛燭曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Xue Zhu said, "It cannot."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu refused.

sentences.zh: 當造此劍之時，赤堇之山破而出錫，若邪之谿涸而出銅，雨師掃灑，雷公擊鼓，太一下觀，天精下之，歐冶乃因天之精，悉其伎巧，一曰純鉤，二曰湛盧。

translations.literal: When these swords were forged, Mount Chijin broke and poured out tin, Ruoye's stream dried and poured out copper; the rain master swept, the thunder duke beat drums, the Grand One looked down from above, heaven's essence descended; Ou Yezi then by heaven's essence, exhausted his skill and cleverness— one day Chunjun, two days Zhanlu."
translations.idiomatic: He told how Ou Yezi forged them when heaven opened Mount Chijin for tin and dried Ruoye for copper, spirits sweeping and drumming while essence fell— making Chunjun and Zhanlu.

sentences.zh: 今赤堇之山已合，若邪之谿深而不測，歐冶子已死，雖傾城量金，珠玉竭河，獨不得此一物。

translations.literal: Now Mount Chijin has closed again, Ruoye's stream is deep and unfathomable, Master Ou Yezi is dead— though you tilt a city to measure gold, pearls and jade exhaust the river, alone you cannot obtain this one thing.
translations.idiomatic: Those mines are sealed, the smith is dead— no heap of gold or pearls can buy such a blade again.

sentences.zh: 有市之鄉三，駿馬千匹，千戶之都二，亦何足言與！」〉

translations.literal: Three market towns, a thousand swift horses, two thousand-household capitals— what are they worth mentioning with!"
translations.idiomatic: Your towns and horses are nothing beside it!"

sentences.zh: 瓠梁托弦以流聲；

translations.literal: Hu Liang entrusted strings thereby to send flowing sound;
translations.idiomatic: Hu Liang drew music from strings,

sentences.zh: 〈《淮南子》曰：瓠巴鼓瑟而鱘魚聽之。

translations.literal: The Huainanzi says: Hu Ba strummed the se and sturgeon fish listened."
translations.idiomatic: the Huainanzi says Hu Ba's se charmed fish from the deep."

sentences.zh: 又曰：瓠梁之歌可隨也，而以歌者不可為也。〉

translations.literal: Again it says: Hu Liang's songs can be followed, yet he who sings them cannot be matched."
translations.idiomatic: It also says anyone may copy Hu Liang's tune, but no one can sing like Hu Liang."

sentences.zh: 齊隸拊髀以濟文，

translations.literal: A Qi bondsman slapped thigh to aid letters,
translations.idiomatic: A Qi retainer slapped his thighs to mimic a cock and save his lord,

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之曰：按此謂孟嘗君田文下坐客，能作雞鳴以濟其厄者也。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi notes: This refers to the seated guest under Lord Mengchang Tian Wen who could make a cock crow to save his peril.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes this is the cock-crow guest who saved Lord Mengchang.

sentences.zh: 凡作雞鳴，必先拊髀，以傚雞之拊翼也。〉

translations.literal: Whenever making cock crow, one must first slap the thigh, to imitate the chicken's slapping wings."
translations.idiomatic: Mimicking a cock begins with slapping the thigh like beating wings."

sentences.zh: 楚客潛寇以保荊：

translations.literal: A Chu guest secretly stole thereby to preserve Jing:
translations.idiomatic: A Chu thief slipped into camp to save the state,

sentences.zh: 〈《淮南子》曰：楚將子發好求技道之士。

translations.literal: The Huainanzi says: Chu general Zi Fa loved to seek men of skill and way.
translations.idiomatic: the Huainanzi tells how general Zi Fa of Chu loved odd talents.

sentences.zh: 楚有善為偷者，往見曰：「聞君求技道之士，臣偷也，原以技備一卒。

translations.literal: Chu had one good at stealing; he went to see saying, "I have heard you seek men of skill and way; your servant is a thief; I wish with skill to fill one soldier."
translations.idiomatic: A thief offered his craft as a soldier's skill.

sentences.zh: 」子發聞之，衣不及帶，冠不暇正，出見而禮之。

translations.literal: Zi Fa heard it; clothes did not reach belt, cap had no time to be straightened; he went out to see and treated him with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Zi Fa rushed out half-dressed to honor him.

sentences.zh: 左右諫曰：「偷者，天下之盜也，何為禮之？

translations.literal: Those at left and right remonstrated saying, "A thief is a robber under heaven— why treat him with ritual?"
translations.idiomatic: His staff protested honoring a thief.

sentences.zh: 」君曰：「此非左右之所得與。

translations.literal: The lord said, "This is not what those at left and right can join in."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "You do not understand."

sentences.zh: 」後無幾何，齊興兵伐楚。

translations.literal: Afterward not long, Qi raised troops to attack Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Qi invaded Chu.

sentences.zh: 子發將師以當之，兵三卻。

translations.literal: Zi Fa led the army to meet them; the army three times retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Zi Fa met them and fell back three times.

sentences.zh: 楚賢大夫皆盡其計而悉其誠，齊師愈強。

translations.literal: Chu's worthy grandees all exhausted their plans and poured out their sincerity; Qi's army grew stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Every Chu stratagem failed while Qi grew stronger.

sentences.zh: 於是卒偷進請曰：「臣有薄技，原為君行之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the foot soldier thief advanced requesting saying, "Your servant has a slight skill; I wish to act it for you, lord."
translations.idiomatic: The thief stepped forward: "Let me use my small skill for you."

sentences.zh: 」君曰「諾」。
