translations.literal: The lord said, "Granted."
translations.idiomatic: The lord agreed.

sentences.zh: 偷即夜出，解齊將軍之帳，而獻之子發。

translations.literal: The thief then at night went out, undid the Qi general's curtain, and presented it to Zi Fa.
translations.idiomatic: That night the thief slipped into the Qi camp, cut loose the general's tent hangings, and brought them to Zi Fa.

sentences.zh: 子發使人歸之，曰：「卒有出採薪者，得將軍之帳，使使歸於執事。

translations.literal: Zi Fa sent men to return them, saying, "A soldier who went out gathering firewood obtained the general's curtain; I send envoys to return it to the commanding officer."
translations.idiomatic: Zi Fa sent them back with word that a foraging soldier had "found" the general's drapery and wished to return it politely.

sentences.zh: 」明日又復往取枕，子發又使歸之。

translations.literal: The next day again he went to take the pillow; Zi Fa again sent it returned.
translations.idiomatic: The next night he stole the pillow; again Zi Fa returned it.

sentences.zh: 明日又復往取簪，子發又使歸之。

translations.literal: The next day again he went to take the hairpin; Zi Fa again sent it returned.
translations.idiomatic: The third night he took the hairpin; again Zi Fa sent it back.

sentences.zh: 齊師聞之大駭，將軍與軍吏謀曰：「今日不去，楚軍恐取吾頭矣！

translations.literal: When Qi's army heard it they were greatly terrified; the general and army officers plotted saying, "If today we do not leave, Chu's army I fear will take our heads!"
translations.idiomatic: The Qi army panicked; the council cried, "If we stay, Chu will have our heads!"

sentences.zh: 」即旋師而去。〉

translations.literal: Thereupon they wheeled the army and departed."
translations.idiomatic: They broke camp and fled."

sentences.zh: 雍門援琴而挾說，

translations.literal: Yongmen Zhou took up the zither and clasped persuasion,
translations.idiomatic: Yongmen Zhou plucked the zither and moved his hearer with argument,

sentences.zh: 〈桓譚《新論》曰：雍門周以琴見，孟嘗君曰：「先生鼓琴，亦能令文悲乎？

translations.literal: Huan Tan's New Discourses states: Yongmen Zhou with the zither had an audience; Lord Mengchang said, "Sir, if you strum the zither, can you also make Wen sorrowful?"
translations.idiomatic: Huan Tan's New Discourses: Yongmen Zhou played for Lord Mengchang, who asked whether music could sadden him.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣之所能令悲者，先貴而後賤，昔富而今貧，擯壓窮巷，不交四鄰；

translations.literal: He answered saying, "What your servant can make sorrowful: first noble then base, once rich now poor, pressed into a poor lane, not befriending the four neighbors;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou listed the fallen noble, the ruined rich man, the recluse shunned by neighbors;

sentences.zh: 不若身材高妙，懷質抱真，逢讒罹謗，怨結而不得信；

translations.literal: or not like one tall in body and subtle, cherishing substance and embracing truth, meeting slander and bearing calumny, resentment knotted yet unable to be believed;
translations.idiomatic: the worthy slandered and disbelieved;

sentences.zh: 不若交歡而結愛，無怨而生離，遠赴絕國，無相見期；

translations.literal: or not like exchanging joy and knotting love, without rancor yet born separation, going far to a cut-off state, no meeting date;
translations.idiomatic: lovers parted without quarrel across endless distance;

sentences.zh: 不若幼無父母，壯無妻兒，出以野澤為鄰，入用堀穴為家，困於朝夕，無所假貸：若此人者，但聞飛烏之號，秋風鳴條，則傷心矣，臣一為之援琴而長太息，未有不淒惻而涕泣者也。

translations.literal: or not like in youth without father and mother, in maturity without wife and children, going out with wild marsh as neighbor, entering with burrow-hole as home, pressed between dawn and dusk, nowhere to borrow: if it is such a person— only hearing flying birds' cry, autumn wind whistling in branches— then his heart is wounded; your servant once for him takes up the zither and long sighs— never is there one who is not mournful and weeping."
translations.idiomatic: the orphan with no kin, homeless between marsh and cave— such a man weeps at wind and birds; I have only to play and he floods with tears."

sentences.zh: 今若足下，居則廣廈高堂，連闥洞房，下羅帷，來清風；

translations.literal: Now as for you, sir, in dwelling then broad halls and high chambers, linked doors and inner chambers, below gauze curtains, clear wind comes;
translations.idiomatic: But you, my lord, live in mansions hung with silk, cooled by breeze,

sentences.zh: 倡優在前，諂諛侍側，揚激楚，舞鄭妾，流聲以娛耳，練色以淫目；

translations.literal: singing girls in front, flatterers attending at the side, raising the fierce Chu airs, dancing Zheng beauties, flowing sound to delight the ear, trained colors to dazzle the eye;
translations.idiomatic: with singers, sycophants, Chu melodies, Zheng dancers— every sense feasted;

sentences.zh: 水戲則舫龍舟，建羽旗，鼓釣乎不測之淵；

translations.literal: in water play then barge dragon boats, raise feather banners, drum and fish in unfathomable depths;
translations.idiomatic: on water you race dragon boats under feather flags;

sentences.zh: 野遊則登平原，馳廣囿，強弩下高鳥，勇士格猛獸；

translations.literal: in wild roaming then ascend the plain, gallop the great park, strong crossbows shoot high birds, brave knights grapple fierce beasts;
translations.idiomatic: on land you hunt the plain with crossbow and spear;

sentences.zh: 置酒娛樂，沈醉忘歸：方此之時，視天地曾不若一指，雖有善鼓琴，未能足下也。

translations.literal: set out wine for pleasure, sink drunk and forget return: at this moment you look on heaven and earth as not even one finger; although there be one good at strumming the zither, he cannot match you, sir."
translations.idiomatic: you drink until heaven and earth seem smaller than your thumb— what player could sadden you?"

sentences.zh: 」孟嘗君曰：「固然！

translations.literal: Lord Mengchang said, "It is indeed so!"
translations.idiomatic: Mengchang agreed.

sentences.zh: 」雍門周曰：「然臣竊為足下有所常悲。

translations.literal: Yongmen Zhou said, "Yet your servant privately for you, sir, has what one constantly mourns."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou answered, "Yet I grieve for you nonetheless."

sentences.zh: 夫角帝而困秦者君也，連五國而伐楚者又君也。

translations.literal: He who cornered the emperor and trapped Qin was you, sir; he who linked five states and attacked Chu was again you, sir."
translations.idiomatic: You humbled Qin and led the league against Chu—

sentences.zh: 天下未嘗無事，不從即衡；

translations.literal: Under heaven there has never been no affair; if not vertical then horizontal;
translations.idiomatic: the world never rests: vertical alliance or horizontal,

sentences.zh: 從成則楚王，衡成則秦帝。

translations.literal: if vertical succeeds then Chu is king; if horizontal succeeds then Qin is emperor."
translations.idiomatic: one makes Chu king, the other makes Qin emperor."

sentences.zh: 夫以秦、楚之強而報弱薛，猶磨蕭斧而伐朝菌也，有識之士，莫不為足下寒心。

translations.literal: Now with Qin and Chu's strength to repay weak Xue— it is like grinding a fragrant axe to cut a morning mushroom; men of insight, none do not for you, sir, chill at heart."
translations.idiomatic: Against Qin or Chu, little Xue is a mushroom under an axe— every thinking man shudders for you.

sentences.zh: 天道不常盛，寒暑更進退，千秋萬歲之後，宗廟必不血食；

translations.literal: Heaven's way is not constantly flourishing; cold and heat advance and retreat; after a thousand autumns and myriad years, the ancestral temple surely will not receive blood sacrifice;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven turns; after ages your line may no longer smell the smoke of sacrifice;

sentences.zh: 高台既已傾，曲池又已平，墳墓生荊棘，狐狸穴其中，遊兒牧豎躑躅其足而歌其上曰：『孟嘗君之尊貴，亦猶若是乎！

translations.literal: high terraces already have tilted, winding pools again have been leveled, tombs grow thorns and brambles, foxes burrow in them; wandering boys and cowherds hobble their feet on them and sing above saying, "Lord Mengchang's honor and nobility— is it also like this!"
translations.idiomatic: your towers will fall, your pools fill in, thorns choke the tombs, and herd boys will sing over your bones, "So passed Lord Mengchang's glory!"

sentences.zh: 』」於是孟嘗君喟然太息，涕淚承睫而未下。

translations.literal: Thereupon Lord Mengchang sighed a long sigh; tears and mucus hung on the lashes yet did not fall.
translations.idiomatic: Mengchang wept until tears hung on his lashes.

sentences.zh: 雍門周引琴而鼓之，徐動宮徵，叩角羽，終而成曲，孟嘗君遂歔欷而就之曰：「先生鼓琴，令文立若亡國之人也。」〉

translations.literal: Yongmen Zhou drew the zither and drummed it, slowly moving gong and zhi, striking jiao and yu, at last completing the tune; Lord Mengchang thereupon sobbed and drew near him saying, "Sir, by your strumming you have made Wen stand like a man of a lost state."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou played a slow, wrenching tune until Mengchang sobbed, "Your music has made me a man of a fallen kingdom."

sentences.zh: 韓哀秉轡而馳名；

translations.literal: Han Ai grasped reins thereby to gallop fame;
translations.idiomatic: Han Ai mastered the chariot and won renown;

sentences.zh: 〈《呂氏春秋》曰：韓哀作禦。

translations.literal: The Lüshi Chunqiu states: Han Ai made charioteering."
translations.idiomatic: the Lüshi Chunqiu credits Han Ai with the art of driving.

sentences.zh: 王褒聖主得賢臣頌曰：及至駕齧膝，參乘旦，王良執靶，韓哀附輿，縱馳騁騖，忽如景靡，過都越國，蹶如歷塊，追奔電，逐遺風，周流八極，萬里一息，何其遼哉！

translations.literal: Wang Bao's Rhapsody on the Sage Ruler Obtaining Worthy Ministers states: Reaching the time when the horse gnaws the knee, the third rider at dawn, Wang Liang holds the whip, Han Ai attends the carriage, letting loose gallop and race, swift as a shadow melting, passing capitals and crossing states, fast as clearing a clod, chasing running lightning, pursuing the fleeing wind, circling the eight poles, ten thousand li in one breath— how vast it is! Man and horse obtain each other."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bao's rhapsody praises Wang Liang and Han Ai: at dawn, whip in hand, they drive so fast they outrun wind and lightning across the realm— man and steed as one."

sentences.zh: 人馬相得也。〉

translations.literal: Man and horse obtain each other."
translations.idiomatic: So runs the praise of their perfect partnership."

sentences.zh: 盧敖翱翔乎玄闕，若士竦身於雲清。

translations.literal: Lu Ao soared in the dark gate; Ru Shi drew body up into cloud clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ao roamed the dark void; the transcendent leapt into the clouds;

sentences.zh: 〈《淮南子》曰：盧敖遊乎北海，經乎太陰，入乎玄闕，至於蒙轂之上，見一士焉，深目而玄準，戾頸而鳶肩，豐上而殺下，軒軒然方迎風而舞，顧見盧敖慢然下其臂，遯逃乎碑下。

translations.literal: The Huainanzi states: Lu Ao roamed in the northern sea, passed through the great yin, entered the dark gate, reached above Menggu, saw a gentleman there, deep eyes and black nose, twisted neck and kite shoulders, broad above and narrow below, loftily facing the wind and dancing; turning he saw Lu Ao and slowly lowered his arms, hiding beneath a stone.
translations.idiomatic: the Huainanzi tells how Lu Ao met a strange being in the far north who hid from him.

sentences.zh: 盧敖俯而視之，方卷龜殼而食合梨。

translations.literal: Lu Ao bent and looked at him; he was just rolling a tortoise shell and eating a pear.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ao peeked and saw him munching a pear on a tortoise shell.

sentences.zh: 盧敖乃與之語曰：「惟敖為背羣離黨，窮觀於六合之外者，非敖而已乎！

translations.literal: Lu Ao then spoke with him saying, "Only Ao has turned his back on the flock and left the party, exhaustively viewing outside the six directions— is it not none but Ao!"
translations.idiomatic: Lu boasted of his lonely travels beyond the world.

sentences.zh: 敖幼而好遊，長不喻解，周行四極，惟北陰之不闚，今卒睹夫子於是，子殆可與敖為交乎！

translations.literal: Ao in youth loved roaming; grown, still not understanding, I have circled the four poles; only the northern yin I have not peered into; now at last I see you, sir, here— you, sir, can almost befriend Ao!"
translations.idiomatic: He said he had seen every pole but the north and now begged friendship.

sentences.zh: 」若士者蠤然而笑曰：「嘻乎！

translations.literal: The gentleman like a cricket laughed saying, "Ha!"
translations.idiomatic: The figure gave a cricket's laugh: "Ha!"

sentences.zh: 子中州民，寧肯而遠至此？

translations.literal: You are a man of the central provinces— how could you have come this far?"
translations.idiomatic: "You are a townsman of the heartland— what brings you here?"

sentences.zh: 此猶光乎日月而戴列星，陰陽之所行，四時之所生，此其比夫不名之地，猶突奧也。

translations.literal: This is still brighter than sun and moon and wearing the arrayed stars, where yin and yang move and the four seasons are born— compared to that unnamed land, it is still like a chimney corner."
translations.idiomatic: "This place still has sun, moon, and seasons— beside the nameless void it is only a chimney nook."

sentences.zh: 若我南游乎罔{罒良}之野，北息於沈墨之鄉，西窮冥冥之黨，東貫鴻濛之光，此其下無地而上無天，聽焉無聞，視焉則眴，此其外猶有沈沈之汜，其餘一舉而千萬里，吾猶未能之在。

translations.literal: As for me, south I roam in the wild of Wangliang, north I rest in the township of dark ink, west I exhaust the party of dim dark, east I pierce the light of primal mist— here below there is no earth and above no heaven, listening there is no sound, looking then it dazzles; outside this there is still a deep deep ford; the rest one leap and a thousand myriad li— I still have not been able to be there.
translations.idiomatic: "I roam voids beyond north, south, east, and west where there is neither sky nor ground— vaster than you can leap in a thousand leagues— and I have not reached their limit."

sentences.zh: 今子遊始至於此，乃語窮觀，豈不亦遠哉！

translations.literal: Now you, sir, your roaming has only reached here, yet you speak of exhaustive viewing— is it not also far!"
translations.idiomatic: "You have barely started yet call yourself a traveler— presumptuous!"

sentences.zh: 然子處矣，吾與汗漫期於九垓之上，吾不可以久。

translations.literal: Yet you, sir, stay; I have an appointment with Hanman on the nine heights above— I cannot stay long."
translations.idiomatic: "Stay if you like; I am due to meet Hanman above the nine heavens— I cannot linger."

sentences.zh: 」若士舉臂而竦身，遂入雲中。

translations.literal: The gentleman raised arms and drew up his body, then entered the clouds.
translations.idiomatic: He stretched and rose into the clouds.

sentences.zh: 盧敖仰而視之，弗見乃止，曰：「吾比夫子也，猶黃鵠之與壤蟲，終日行不離咫尺，自以為遠，不亦悲哉！」〉

translations.literal: Lu Ao looked up and watched him; not seeing him he stopped, saying, "Compared to that gentleman, I am like a yellow swan to a soil worm— all day walking not leaving a foot and inch, myself thinking it far— is it not also sorrowful!"
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ao cried, "Beside him I am a mayfly beside a swan— pathetic!"

sentences.zh: 余實不能齊技於數子，故乃靜然守己而自寧。」

translations.literal: I truly cannot equal my skill with these several men; therefore I am quiet and guard myself and find peace."
translations.idiomatic: I cannot match those masters; I keep still and find peace in myself."

sentences.zh: 景耀六年，後主從譙周之計，遣使請降於鄧艾。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jingyao, the Later Lord followed Qiao Zhou's plan, sent an envoy to request surrender from Deng Ai.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyao 6 the Later Lord adopted Qiao Zhou's counsel and sent Deng Ai terms of surrender.

sentences.zh: 其書，正所造也。

translations.literal: That document was what Zheng composed.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zheng had drafted that letter.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，鐘會作亂成都，後主東遷洛陽，時擾攘倉卒。

translations.literal: The next year first month, Zhong Hui made rebellion in Chengdu; the Later Lord moved east to Luoyang; at the time it was tumultuous and hasty.
translations.idiomatic: The next New Year Zhong Hui mutinied at Chengdu; the court moved east to Luoyang in chaos.

sentences.zh: 蜀之大臣無冀從者，惟正及殿中督汝南張通，捨妻子單身隨侍。

translations.literal: Shu's great ministers had none who hoped to follow; only Zheng and palace guard Zhang Tong of Runan, casting aside wife and children, alone in body followed and attended.
translations.idiomatic: No great officer chose exile with the sovereign except Xi Zheng and Zhang Tong, who abandoned their families to go.

sentences.zh: 後主賴正相導宜適，舉動無闕，乃慨然歎息，恨知正之晚，時論嘉之。

translations.literal: The Later Lord relied on Zheng to guide what was fitting and appropriate; movements and actions had no fault; then he sighed with feeling, regretting knowing Zheng late; opinion of the time praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord leaned on Zheng for deportment at the Wei court and sighed that he had known him too late; contemporaries praised them both.

sentences.zh: 賜爵關內候。

translations.literal: He was granted noble rank marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed marquis within the passes.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，除安陽令，遷巴西太守。

translations.literal: In Taishi he was appointed magistrate of Anyang, transferred to administrator of Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jin he became magistrate of Anyang, then prefect of Ba.

sentences.zh: 泰始八年詔曰：「正昔在成都，顛沛守義，不違忠節，及見受用，盡心幹事，有治理之績，其以正為巴西太守。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taishi an edict said, "Zheng in old days at Chengdu, in overturning preserved righteousness, did not violate loyal integrity; when received and employed, he exhausted heart in managing affairs and had traces of good order— appoint Zheng administrator of Ba."
translations.idiomatic: A Taishi 8 edict cited his loyalty in Shu and his good work as prefect of Ba.

sentences.zh: 」咸寧四年卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianning he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Xianning.

sentences.zh: 凡所著述詩論賦之屬，垂百篇。

translations.literal: In all that he authored— poems, disquisitions, rhapsodies of that class— nearly a hundred pieces.
translations.idiomatic: His writings— verse, essays, rhapsodies— number nearly a hundred.

sentences.zh: 評曰：杜微脩身隱靜，不役當世，庶幾夷、皓之槩。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Du Wei cultivated the person and hid in stillness, not serving the age— he was almost of the mold of Bo Yi and the four hoary recluses.
translations.idiomatic: Du Wei lived in seclusion like the ancient recluses.

sentences.zh: 周羣佔天有徵，杜瓊沈默慎密，諸生之純也。

translations.literal: Zhou Qun divined heaven and had verification; Du Qiong was silent and careful— they were purity among scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Qun read the sky truly; Du Qiong was reserved and exact— models of scholarly integrity.

sentences.zh: 許、孟、來、李，博涉多聞，尹默精於左氏，雖不以德業為稱，信皆一時之學士。

translations.literal: Xu, Meng, Lai, Li— broad-ranging and much hearing; Yin Mo was refined in the Zuo tradition; although they were not famed for virtue and enterprise, truly all were scholars of their time.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ci, Meng Guang, Lai Min, and Li were encyclopedic; Yin Mo mastered the Zuo commentary— none were famed as moral paragons, yet all were leading scholars.

sentences.zh: 譙周詞理淵通，為世碩儒，有董、揚之規，郤正文辭燦爛，有張、蔡之風，加其行止，君子有取焉。

translations.literal: Qiao Zhou's words and pattern were deep and penetrating; he was a great Confucian of the age, having the measure of Dong Zhongshu and Yang Xiong; Xi Zheng's letters and phrases were brilliant, having the air of Zhang Heng and Cai Yong; add their conduct— the gentleman has what to take from them.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zhou's learning matched Dong and Yang; Xi Zheng's prose matched Zhang and Cai— and their lives offer lessons worth keeping.

sentences.zh: 二子處晉事少，在蜀事多，故著於篇。

translations.literal: The two sons had little to do with Jin affairs and much with Shu affairs; therefore they are set down in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou and Zheng belong chiefly to Shu's story, so they fill this scroll.

sentences.zh: 〈張璠以為譙周所陳降魏之策，蓋素料劉禪懦弱，心無害戾，故得行也。

translations.literal: Zhang Fan thought that the plan Qiao Zhou presented to surrender to Wei— in general he had long reckoned Liu Shan weak and soft, his heart without harmful perversity, therefore it could be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fan argues Zhou knew Liu Shan too gentle to punish dissent, so surrender was safe.

sentences.zh: 如遇忿肆之人，雖無他算，然矜殉鄙恥，或發怒妄誅，以立一時之威，快其斯須之意者，此亦夷滅之禍云。〉

translations.literal: If he had met a man furious and unrestrained, although without other schemes, yet proud of martyrdom and shaming disgrace, or perhaps in anger rashly executing to establish a moment's awe, gratifying the thought of that instant— this too is the calamity of extinction and wiping out, it is said."
translations.idiomatic: Had Shan been a violent tyrant, he might have killed Zhou for shaming him— and brought ruin on all."
